rows.title: Generalize: wire IMM-11 fillable-PDF prefill to the UI for DE/FR corridors (real gov PDFs)
rows.notes:
## Decomposed into 5 subtasks on 2026-08-04

1. Source + upload the real DE/FR government AcroForm PDFs — Ready for AI, 🔴 Red, Human Only
2. Seed real form_field_mappings from the authentic field names — Blocked on 1, 🔴 Red
3. Make generate-form corridor-generic (drop the blue_card default) — Ready for AI, 🟡 Yellow
4. Wire the dossier UI action + per-field fill report — Blocked on 3, 🟡 Yellow
5. Golden DE + FR end-to-end fill cases — Blocked on 1–4, 🔴 Red

## Triage verdict: DECOMPOSE (scope endorsed, not superseded)
FINDINGS.md Appendix A.1 does NOT retire this task — it confirms it: "restrict any AcroForm-PDF prefill to corridors that genuinely use fillable paper forms (DE/FR)". Open decisions F1/F2 (§6.1) are resolved in this task's favour. Norway stays on the data-sheet model, which subtask 3 and 4 both assert explicitly.

## Premises verified against tree + prod, not assumed
- Real gov PDFs absent: seed_immigration_form_templates.py:4 builds SYNTHETIC AcroForm stand-ins; prod has 83 form_templates but only 1 with original_pdf_url, and 27 form_field_mappings.
- Frontend genuinely unwired: grep -rln 'available-forms|generate-form' frontend/src returns NOTHING. The IMM-11 backend has been live and reachable for months with no user-facing entry point.
- Not corridor-generic: immigration_forms.py:66 — visa_type: str = "blue_card", so a FR case omitting visa_type receives the GERMAN form.
- The dossier UI already exists (EmployeeDossierPage.tsx, HrCaseDossierPage.tsx, api/dossier.ts), so subtask 4 extends rather than builds — and the "AFTER the FR→NO slice" dependency is softer than the brief implies.

## Dropped from the parent's scope
The brief lists "dual-router-registration gates apply" as outstanding. It is already satisfied — both handlers are registered in backend/main.py:900 AND backend/app/main.py:206 (verified). Made a non-regression assertion inside subtask 3 instead of a subtask of its own.

## Sequencing rationale
The authentic PDFs gate everything factual — field names cannot be mapped (2) or asserted (5) until real forms exist — so subtask 1 blocks both. Subtask 3 is deliberately parallel: dropping the blue_card default needs no PDF, so it must not wait. Subtask 5 is separate from 2 because "mappings seeded" and "a real case fills correctly" fail independently: a mapping can name a valid AcroForm field and still pull the wrong source value.

## Human gate on subtask 1 (deliberate)
Subtask 1 is marked Human Only. Deciding that a given file is the current, authentic government form is a provenance judgement, not a coding task — an agent fetching a plausible CERFA from a search result would put fabricated authority behind every downstream fill, and FINDINGS §2 explicitly ranks accuracy above wiring. Romain supplies or approves the source; the subtask carries the AcroForm-enumeration check that rejects a flattened or scanned PDF before it is accepted.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: docs

rows.title: Fix admin health rollup: no-data≠healthy; reconcile overview vs executive
rows.notes:
SHIPPED in PR #1826, merged 2026-08-12.

## The bug, confirmed at its root

The overview card counted health as !m.alert.firing. A metric that has never been evaluated also does not fire — backend/app/services/rag_eval_reports.py:208 returns {"firing": false, "reason": "no_data"} — so "never measured" and "measured and fine" were indistinguishable. On an empty dataset the card read 3/3 healthy.

## The fix

  healthy  = reason != 'no_data' AND not firing
  measured = reason != 'no_data'            <- the honest denominator
  summary  = healthy / MEASURED, or the word "Unmeasured" when measured == 0

Dividing by TOTAL was the second half of the bug: it averages an unmeasured metric into the score rather than excluding it. When nothing has been evaluated the card now says "Unmeasured" rather than "0/0", because 0/0 still reads as a number you can glance past. Unmeasured metrics get their own row, so the gap is visible instead of hidden in a ratio.

## Scope checked, not assumed

The ticket asked to reconcile overview vs executive. Checked every site using alert.firing before touching anything: AdminRagQualityPage counts firing (alerting, not health) and is CORRECT, and ExecutiveDashboardPage computes no RAG health at all. AdminOverviewPage:128 was the only site, so there was nothing to reconcile — the two pages did not disagree, one of them was simply wrong.

## Validation

Both new tests were verified RED against origin/main before being kept — source reverted, 2 failed / 3 passed confirmed, then restored:
- healthy + failing + no_data must render 1/2, never 2/3
- three no_data must render "Unmeasured", never 3/3 or 0/0

Frontend suite: 251 files / 1752 tests pass. tsc clean.

## Two mistakes worth recording

Both produce tests that pass while proving nothing:
1. The first "Unmeasured" assertion passed trivially, because "Unmeasured" was also the label I had given the new row — the string was present regardless of the metric value. The row is now "Metrics not yet measured".
2. The test helper waited only for the card to EXIST, which is immediate since it renders a loading skeleton first. It now waits for the headline metric to settle.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.title: Roadmap paywall bypass on direct URL load — render gate trusts /api/payment/status boolean (fails open on assignment-id) instead of the authoritative 402
rows.notes:
## What was built
Closed the roadmap paywall bypass on direct URL load. Reproduced on prod with capture; the CLIENT render-gate failed OPEN. PR #1660 (branch fix/roadmap-paywall-direct-load, SHA 54353176).

## Reproduced (captured, unpaid staged FR_NO case)
- GET /api/payment/status/{caseId} → 200 {access_tier:'free', roadmap_unlocked:false} (server correct).
- GET /api/payment/status/{assignmentId} → 404 {"detail":"Case not found"}.
- The server does NOT return roadmap_unlocked=true; the fail-open is the CLIENT: fetchRoadmapUnlocked had catch { return true }. Direct-load roadmap URLs carry the ASSIGNMENT id (the checkout success_url is /employee/case/{assignmentId}/roadmap) → 404 → catch → true → unpaid roadmap rendered.

## Fix (fail CLOSED)
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/utils/paymentStatus.ts — fetchRoadmapUnlocked now returns false on no caseId or any error (404/network). This is the authoritative-fail-closed entitlement check this ticket asked for; a false lock is recoverable, a free €800 roadmap is not.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/utils/paymentStatus.test.ts — the two fail-OPEN assertions inverted to fail-CLOSED + a 404 case.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/routers/payment.py + backend/tests/test_payment_checkout.py — an endpoint-level resolver so GET /status/{id} accepts a case_id OR assignment_id and returns the real (locked) status instead of 404.

## ⚠️ OVERLAP the reviewer must resolve
The server-side half of PR #1660 (the payment.py assignment-id resolver) OVERLAPS the still-OPEN PR #1654 / AIQ-1687, which fixes the SAME server 404 differently (widening require_case_access's assignment lookup, 45 call sites). Two competing server fixes — only one should merge. Recommendation: trim PR #1660 to the CLIENT fail-closed fix only (which cleanly owns THIS ticket) and let PR #1654 own the server-side assignment-id resolution (AIQ-1687). If #1654 merges, my payment.py resolver becomes redundant and would even report case_id = assignmentId cosmetically (require_case_access would succeed on the raw id). #1652 (resolve_entitlement by assignment id) is already merged.

## Validation results
- ✅ Client: vitest paymentStatus → 5 passed (fail-closed on no-id / error / 404). tsc clean.
- ✅ Server: pytest test_payment_checkout → 9 passed (case unpaid locks; assignment-id unpaid locks not-404; assignment-id PAID unlocks; unknown id 404s).
- Acceptance 1–6 met by the two fixes together (paid case still unlocks on both paths via the server resolver / #1654).

## Known gap (residual, NOT fixed here — see follow-up ticket)
payment.py payment_status still computes unlocked = ... or ent is None or ..., so a case with NO entitlement row unlocks even with the paywall on — a backend fail-open. The FRONTEND half of that residual (any-error → unlocked) IS now closed by this PR; the backend ent is None half remains. Filed as a separate follow-up.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Decide the server-fix overlap (#1660 payment.py resolver vs #1654) — recommend trimming #1660 to client-only.
2. Merge the client fail-closed change; after deploy, direct-load an unpaid roadmap by BOTH case id and assignment id → paywall; paid case → unlocks on both.

rows.title: HR resolved-policy endpoint 500s (KeyError: 'id') for config-matrix companies
rows.notes:
## What was built
Fixed the two HR resolved-policy endpoints that 500'd for config-matrix companies. get_hr_resolved_policy and recompute_resolved_policy both indexed resolved["id"] to re-query resolved_assignment_policy_benefits/_exclusions. Config-matrix resolutions (every test-drive company, and real companies on the config-matrix authoring path) are NOT persisted to resolved_assignment_policies — they carry benefits inline and have no top-level id — so both raised KeyError: 'id' → HTTP 500.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/main.py — get_hr_resolved_policy (~L7644) and recompute_resolved_policy (~L7685): guard the benefit/exclusion re-query on resolved.get("id"). Legacy (persisted) resolution keeps the DB re-query unchanged; config-matrix (no id) uses the inline resolved["benefits"]/["exclusions"]. No persistence, no key aliasing (this is a raw HR resolved-policy view, not the Services-category lookup).

## Validation results
- ✅ cd backend && pytest tests/ -k 'resolved_policy or hr_policy or resolv' — 255 passed / 3 pre-existing env flakes (test_assignment_route_cities ×2, test_p3_exception_wiring — prod-DB/ordering flakes unrelated to this endpoint).
- ✅ LIVE (config-matrix test-drive assignment e2b56ed1…): GET /api/hr/assignments/{id}/resolved-policy → HTTP 200, has_policy=true, source=policy_config_matrix, 31 inline benefits (was 500/KeyError).
- ✅ LIVE: POST /api/hr/assignments/{id}/resolved-policy/recompute → HTTP 200, has_policy=true, 31 benefits.
- ✅ Legacy path unchanged: the id-present branch is byte-identical to the prior code (only the no-id branch is new), so legacy-policy companies re-query as before. (No legacy test-drive company on hand to click live; logically unaffected.)

## Decisions made
- Did NOT apply _with_legacy_benefit_key_aliases here. That aliasing is specific to the Services-category lookup (AIQ-1631); this endpoint returns a raw resolved-policy dump for HR, where duplicating benefit rows under legacy keys would be misleading. The minimal correct fix is: inline benefits, guard the id.

## What the reviewer should do
1. As HR on a config-matrix (test-drive) company, GET /api/hr/assignments/{assignment_id}/resolved-policy → confirm 200 with has_policy=true + benefits (not 500).
2. Confirm a legacy-policy company's HR resolved-policy still returns its persisted benefits unchanged.

rows.title: HR payer view — compare all offers, best-value recommendation, validate the offer
No CI job runs the Edge Function tests — the case-summary PII no-leak gate is unenforced
rows.notes:
## What was built
CI now runs the Supabase Edge Function Deno tests on every PR that touches supabase/functions/**. The case-summary PII whitelist — the automated half of the GDPR "no raw PII in an LLM payload" rule — is enforced by the pipeline instead of by whoever remembered to run deno locally.

PR #1665, squash-merged as 5b8a9a81. Branch ci/aiq-1702-deno-edge-function-tests.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: .github/workflows/ci.yml — added an edge_functions output + supabase/functions/** filter to the existing "Detect changes" dorny/paths-filter job, and a new Edge Function tests (Deno) job gated on it (denoland/setup-deno@v2, pinned v2.1.4, running deno test --no-check=remote supabase/functions/).
- MODIFIED: supabase/functions/case-summary/index.test.ts — header note recording that CI now runs this file and why the job exists. Deliberate double duty: it also places the PR inside the new filter so the job ran on its own change rather than skipping.

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) The job runs (not skipped) on a PR touching `supabase/functions/ and passes.** On PR #1665 Edge Function tests (Deno): success, CI log: ok | 15 passed | 0 failed (6ms). Confirms the filter fires.
- ✅ **2) TEETH — proven in CI, not only locally.** Local (pinned Deno 2.1.4, identical command): adding "notes" to OPERATIONAL_IMMIGRATION_FIELDS → AssertionError: milestone leaked forbidden key: notes, FAILED | 13 passed | 2 failed, non-zero exit. I then pushed that tamper as commit 8851cabd because a local failure does not prove the *job wiring* propagates it — a stray continue-on-error or || true would swallow it. CI result: **Edge Function tests (Deno): failure**, log ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1. Reverted (0d1682fa); CI returned to success / 15 passed | 0 failed, and git diff 51d40f3c HEAD is empty, so the revert was exact.
- ✅ **3) Skips on PRs that don't touch Edge Functions.** On #1665 (which touches neither frontend nor backend) Frontend, Backend tests, E2E, Lighthouse, Route-auth audit, RLS coverage, Migration drift, Storage bucket, HR Dashboard all reported **skipped** — the same filter mechanism, exercised in the excluding direction. ⚠️ The literal wording ("a PR touching only frontend/ runs no Deno job") can only be observed on the next frontend PR; the gating expression is identical in form to the existing frontend / backend` jobs, so no separate PR was burned to prove it.
- ✅ 4) Deno version pinned, not latest: deno-version: v2.1.4.
- ✅ 5) All 15 case-summary tests pass in CI. Log line: ok | 15 passed | 0 failed (6ms). Actionlint (workflow YAML): success also validated the new job's YAML.

## Decisions made
- deno test supabase/functions/ (the whole directory), not the single case-summary path. deno test <dir> discovers every *.test.ts beneath it, so a future function's suite is covered with no edit here — which is what the task's constraint asked for. Today case-summary/index.test.ts is the only suite present.
- --no-check=remote. Local files are still type-checked (the run logs Check file://…index.test.ts); this only skips type-checking the remote deno.land/std modules, which are not ours and would add latency plus a third-party flake surface.
- Tests only — no deno lint / deno check job. The task scoped this to CI wiring for the tests. Adding lint would risk failing on pre-existing issues in the other, untested functions and widen the change.
- Installed Deno 2.1.4 locally to validate before pushing rather than iterating through CI — the same version the job pins, so the local and CI results are comparable.
- Spent two extra CI runs on the teeth check deliberately. Actions minutes are metered here, but a compliance gate that runs and cannot fail is worse than no gate: it reads as coverage. That seemed worth ~2 runs.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Nothing is required — merged and green. To sanity-check the gate yourself: on any branch add a field from FORBIDDEN_PII_FIELDS to a whitelist in supabase/functions/case-summary/summary.ts, push, and confirm Edge Function tests (Deno) goes red.
2. On the next frontend-only PR, glance at the checks and confirm Edge Function tests (Deno) is skipped (no wasted minutes).

## Known gaps / follow-up
- case-summary is the only Edge Function with any tests at all. The other ~25 functions on the project (submit-demo-request, support-triage, pre-call-brief, nightly-stats, …) have no suites, so the new job covers them vacuously. - CREATED: backend/app/services/test_drive_corridor.py — single source of truth for the 5 locked routes + resolve_test_drive_route(user), resolving the acting @probe.test account (HR or employee) → its session's corridor. Returns None for every real user.

- MODIFIED: frontend/src/api/testDrive.ts — exported getTestDriveSession().

## Validation results
- ✅ Test-drive HR/employee sees origin+destination pre-filled and locked — the case is stamped at assign, which lights up the intake's existing "🔒 HR pre-filled" prefill/lock machinery; origin added to the lock set; unlock hatch withheld.
- ✅ Tampered corridor still lands on the ASSIGNED corridor — server-side override in patch_case, verified by test (submit BR→JP, case persists IN→DE / ES→AE).
- ✅ Never a test-drive case outside the 5 locked corridors — the route map contains only those five and is shared with the provisioner whitelist; an unknown corridor_id resolves to None (tested).
- ✅ test_sessions.corridor_id matches the created case's corridor — the stamp reads the session's own corridor_id; parametrised across FR_NO / IN_DE / GB_US so a FR_NO-only regression cannot pass.

### What actually happens
Config-matrix companies (every test-drive case, and real companies on the config-matrix authoring path) have NO legacy company_policies row, so in _resolve_published_policy_for_employee (backend/main.py) pub is None and they return early from the if not pub: matrix-fallback branch (~L9782). They NEVER reach resolve_policy_for_assignment or the branch my first commit (f154aae3) added — that branch was dead code, and has_policy was already True via the fallback all along.

The real defect: the matrix-fallback path returned benefits keyed by their config-matrix names (host_housing_cap, shipment_of_goods, …), but build_employee_services_policy_context / the Services cards look benefits up by the legacy vocabulary (SERVICE_TO_BENEFIT: living_areas → temporary_housing). Without aliasing, every category fell through to “No policy rule” even when a cap was covered.

### Fix shipped (commit 058255fb, supersedes f154aae3)
- MODIFIED backend/main.py _resolve_published_policy_for_employee: apply _with_legacy_benefit_key_aliases to the matrix benefits in the fallback path before returning (mirrors the comparison service); removed the dead branch f154aae3 added.

rows.title: Build accreditation-registry harvester for FR-DE / FR-NO supplier coverage gaps
rows.notes:
## DECISION: key SET — 2026-08-11

Romain generated IMMIGRATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY and set it on the rolec-eu service env tab, then redeployed. Verified end to end against production the same day. The vault is live.

## Validation results (Expected Output items 2 and 3)

2. A passport is stored as ciphertext, not plaintext, not null — PASSED.
Through the real product path (PUT /api/employee/cases/{id}/profile → upsert_profile_employee, which encrypts at immigration_intake_profile.py:380), synthetic value ZZ9999999:


stored_prefix               \xc30d04     (OpenPGP magic — genuine pgcrypto output)
stored_len                  152
is_plaintext                false
plaintext_substring_present false
field_sources_kind          object


A decrypt attempt with a deliberately wrong key raised 39000: Wrong key or corrupt data, which independently confirms the column holds real ciphertext rather than anything that merely looks encrypted.

3. The employee-facing endpoint returns the decrypted value — PASSED.
GET /api/employee/cases/{id}/profile returned passport_number: 'ZZ9999999'. Encrypt → store → decrypt works through the production stack.

1. Decision recorded with a date — this note.

## Two defects found while verifying, both fixed

AIQ-1800b — every write to imm_employee_profiles was 500ing (PR #1786, merged).
The first verification attempt failed with ProgrammingError: can't adapt type 'dict'. field_sources is jsonb and all SIX write paths bound a raw Python dict — HR update, HR insert, employee update, employee insert, and both OCR paths. psycopg2 cannot adapt a dict, so no branch ever worked.

This corrects a premise this ticket was written on. "0 rows, so this is the cheap moment" was read as nothing stored yet. It actually meant nothing could be stored at all — the table had never accepted a row in production, with or without a key. It was also silently blocking AIQ-1790, whose passport UI had shipped hours earlier into a write path that could not succeed.

The plaintext-leak invariant test was itself broken (PR #1783).
It used passport_number NOT LIKE '\\x%'. In LIKE, backslash is the default ESCAPE character, so that pattern means "a literal x followed by anything" — it never matches real ciphertext, so the guard flagged every genuine encrypted row as a leak. It passed only because the table was empty, and would have started crying wolf on the first real passport. Now left(passport_number, 2) <> '\\x', proven in three states: ciphertext-only passes, a planted plaintext row fails with the incident message, removing it goes green.

## Step 0 — the round-trip proof (PR #1783)

Before the key went live, backend/tests/integration/test_vault_passport_roundtrip.py proved the encrypt → store-in-a-text-column → decrypt round trip on real Postgres. This mattered: pg_cast has no bytea→text entry, and every prior vault test mocked the database, so the happy path had never executed anywhere. Without it the first real passport would have been the experiment, on Article 9 data, in production.

Seven tests: pgcrypto present · no bytea→text cast (pins the fragile assumption) · ciphertext survives the text column · same against the real table · wrong key RAISES rather than returning garbage · encryption is non-deterministic · no plaintext rows exist. Runs against a throwaway local Postgres (docker recipe in the docstring), not prod.

## Cleanup

imm_employee_profiles is back to 0 rows, 0 with a passport. The synthetic consent row could not be deleted — consent_records is append-only by trigger, which is correct for a consent audit trail — so a withdrawal row was inserted per the table's own contract. Both rows are on an is_test / @probe.test case, so e2e_purge.py reaps them on its normal schedule.

## Side finding, not fixed here

_check_consent (immigration_service.py) filters consented = TRUE AND withdrawn_at IS NULL before ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1. So inserting a withdrawal row — the mechanism the append-only trigger explicitly instructs you to use — does not actually revoke consent: the original consented=true row still satisfies the filter. Worth its own ticket; it has GDPR consequences and is out of scope for this one.

## Now unblocked

- AIQ-1798 — GDPR export decrypt-or-omit. The key is live, so the "decrypt" branch is now testable rather than hypothetical.
- AIQ-1799 — intake-profile overlay ciphertext bug.
- AIQ-1790 — passport UI. Its write path only started working with #1786.

## Key custody

The passphrase is in Romain's password manager. pgp_sym has no key escrow: losing it makes all stored passport numbers permanently unreadable. Rotation is still cheap at 0 rows and stops being cheap on first real use.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.notes:
## What was built
The first-login welcome dismissal is now owned by profiles.welcome_seen_at and mirrored into localStorage at login, so it survives a change of browser or device. useWelcomeRedirect is completely unchanged and still synchronous — that was the design goal, not an accident.

PR #1669, branch fix/aiq-1701-welcome-seen-cross-device, commit 6a754db6. Contains a migration — apply out-of-band before merging.

## ⚠️ Tier correction (mid-execution)
I authored this ticket as 🟡 Yellow / P3 / Low from a code read. Recon proved that wrong: you cannot know on device B that the user dismissed on device A without server state, and the only correct fix needs a schema migration + a change to the login response — both 🔴 Red per the rubric. I stopped and re-tiered rather than doing Red work under a Yellow badge; Romain approved the plan before any code was written. Ticket re-tiered to 🔴 Red / Medium.

## Files changed
- CREATED: supabase/migrations/20261006000000_profiles_welcome_seen_at.sql — additive nullable welcome_seen_at timestamptz. Timestamp chosen above the prod ledger max (20261005000000), not the repo dir max.
- MODIFIED: backend/schemas.py — UserResponse.welcome_seen: bool = False.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/routers/auth.py — login carries welcome_seen; new POST /api/auth/welcome-seen on the existing auth router.
- MODIFIED: backend/db/users.py — mark_welcome_seen(), idempotent via COALESCE.
- CREATED: backend/tests/test_welcome_seen.py — 6 tests.
- CREATED: frontend/src/api/welcome.ts — persistWelcomeSeen().
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/utils/welcomeSeen.ts — seedWelcomeSeenFromLogin(); MODIFIED frontend/src/utils/welcomeSeen.test.ts — 4 new tests.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts — seeds in setSession (covers login, register and passkey/token-exchange).
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/types.ts; MODIFIED frontend/src/pages/hr/HrWelcomePage.tsx (3 dismiss sites) and frontend/src/pages/employee/EmployeeWelcomePage.tsx (2).

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) Dismiss in browser A → not shown in browser B. seeds a fresh browser when the server says the user already dismissed it.
- ✅ 2) Genuinely new user still sees it once. leaves a genuinely new user unseeded.
- ✅ 3) Storage blocked / lookup fails → SKIPPED, not forced. Pre-existing welcomeSeen.ts:17 fallback untouched; new helper asserted not to throw on blocked storage.
- ✅ 4) Existing localStorage users not re-onboarded. never CLEARS an existing flag when the server reports false — covers false, null, undefined.
- ✅ 5) No flash/bounce. useWelcomeRedirect is byte-for-byte unchanged and still synchronous; the async work happens at login, not on the role home. This is why the seed-at-login design was chosen over an async gate.
- ✅ 6) Existing tests pass. The 3 named files → 19 passed.
- ✅ 7) tsc --noEmit clean; full vitest → 1684 passed / 0 failed. Backend -k "welcome or auth or profile" → 261 passed; full backend → 5619 passed (14 failures = documented pre-existing llm_client baseline).
- ✅ Real Postgres (constraint): rollback-transaction test proved the DDL applies, the UPDATE sets the timestamp, a second dismissal does not move it (COALESCE), and an unknown id touches 0 rows. Verified afterwards that welcome_seen_at still does not exist in prod — the transaction rolled back cleanly.
- ✅ Teeth: the naive setItem(key, seen ? '1' : '0') fails criterion 4's guard. Restored → green.

## Decisions made
- Seed at login rather than an async gate. The constraints flagged async-in-the-mount-effect as the main correctness risk. The login handler already loads the profile row, so the flag rides along at zero extra query cost and the hook never changes.
- Endpoint on the existing auth router — already mounted in both app instances, so the dual-registration trap cannot apply. Asserted against backend.main anyway.
- No request body; the id comes from the token, so one account can never dismiss another's welcome.
- Deploy-order safe. mark_welcome_seen catches ProgrammingError/OperationalError and returns persisted: false, so between deploy and migration-apply the feature degrades to today's behaviour instead of 500-ing every dismissal.
- Kept welcomeSeen.ts dependency-free. api/client.ts imports signOutSupabase; importing it from that util would have dragged Supabase into its jsdom test (a known trap here). The API call lives in the pages instead.
- Rejected stuffing the flag into profiles.notification_prefs (jsonb, already exists) to avoid the migration. It would have kept the task Yellow, but it is a notifications column — misleading to every future reader.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Apply the migration out-of-band, then merge. (PR is deliberately not merged.)
2. Log in, dismiss the welcome, then log in as the same user in incognito → straight to the role home.
3. Confirm a brand-new user still sees it exactly once.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- A test caught a real bug in my own helper: uuid.UUID(None) raises TypeError, not ValueError, so the guard needed widening. The sibling get_profile_record has the same narrow catch and the same latent crash — flagged, deliberately not changed here (out of scope).
- Legacy non-UUID user ids have no profiles row, so their dismissal stays browser-local. Correct degradation, not a regression — but those accounts do not get the cross-device benefit.
- The per-assignment rp_welcome_dismissed:* card flag (AIQ-1269b) is untouched, per the constraints.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.title: AIQ-1795 is NOT closed: ES/NL family templates carry the same defect and the new honesty guard is blind to them
rows.notes:
## Fixed and live — 2026-08-11

Merged as 9554a8ed (PR #1782), migration 20261025000000_fam_reunion_eea_gate_es_nl_no.sql applied to production and ledger reconciled. Ledger max 20261025000000, 442 rows.

## What shipped

1. All six templates gated — ES-FAM-SPOUSE, ES-FAM-CHILD, NL-FAM-SPOUSE, NL-FAM-CHILD, UTL-2011F, UTL-2011B. Each now carries 4 rules, one per non-EEA visa_type.
2. Classifier fixed by category, not by adding nouns — _PERMIT_CATEGORIES now includes family. A name allowlist fails on the next language; there is always a next language.
3. superseded_codes fixed — it matched only WHERE code = 'X', so the batched code IN (...) rewrite was invisible and all six would have been reported as unfixed forever. Same class of mistake as the classifier: keyed on incidental syntax rather than meaning.
4. Corpus extended — 3 new violations (ES/NL/NO, each with its legal basis: RD 240/2007, Vreemdelingenwet/Directive 2004/38/EC, utlendingsloven kap. 13) and 1 new clean case (NL-BSN) to pin that widening to family did not drag registration steps in.

## The visa_type list was not a judgement call

Resolved by reading trigger_engine, not by copying DE's list: _purpose_to_visa_type maps exactly four purposes (work→skilled_worker, intra_company_transfer, family_join, remote_work) and eea_registration is the only other value _build_context can return. One rule per non-EEA visa_type is the exhaustive complement.

Accepted trade: a case whose purpose maps to NULL on a non-EEA corridor now matches no rule and gets no family template. Fail-closed — silence rather than a false requirement — the same trade AIQ-1795/1795b already made.

## Validation — every criterion met

1. ✅ Guard exits 1 naming all six before the migration; 0 after.
2. ✅ Exits 0 with the migration present (all six correctly deferred, not silently dropped).
3. ✅ is_permit_like('Family reunification - child', 'family') → True.
4. ✅ Class-wide live query: 0 family-category templates ungated on an EEA destination — checked against all 30 EEA countries, not just ES/NL/NO.
5. ✅ Renaming no longer matters — test_the_german_templates_would_still_be_caught_if_renamed asserts is_permit_like('', 'family') is True.

Non-vacuity proven: reverting the classifier fails 3 tests, including corpus recall.

Pre-apply simulation: ran the UPDATE's expression read-only against the live rows first and confirmed 4 rules per template, 0 ungated, with priority (ES/NL 85/84, NO 90), event, for_persons and the has_spouse/has_children flags all preserved. The migration rewrites each rule in place rather than restating it, so those cannot be mis-transcribed.

Both CI pytest calls green: 6147 passed / 24 passed.

## Note

RLS coverage check failed on the PR — pre-existing repo-wide gate on the policy-less public.exception_requests table, which fails every migration-touching PR (#1775 and #1778 both merged with it). Verified the table is not anon-readable (no SELECT grant), so it is not an exposure — but a permanently-red security gate trains people to ignore it and is worth its own task.

rows.title: E2E regression: welcome dismissal survives a new device (hermetic Playwright)
rows.notes:
## What was built
A hermetic Playwright spec that codifies AIQ-1701's headline promise — a returning user on a NEW browser is not re-onboarded. That criterion passed review by code inspection only; the sole confirmation was a manual incognito login. It is now a PR-gating test.

PR #1674, branch test/aiq-1711-welcome-persistence-e2e, commit 83869156. Test-only — no app code, no schema, no prod change.

## Files changed
- CREATED: frontend/e2e/welcome.persistence.spec.ts — 4 tests (2 cases × HR + EMPLOYEE).

No other file touched. frontend/e2e/support/mockApi.ts was reused as-is; it needed no login fixture extension because the mocked response is defined inline in the spec's helper.

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) npx playwright test welcome.persistence passes locally — 4 passed, 0 failed.
- ✅ 2) Case A — welcome_seen:true → no re-onboarding, both roles. Asserts toHaveURL(role home) then, after a settle, not.toHaveURL(/\/(hr|employee)\/welcome/). The negative is checked against ANY welcome route, so a wrong-role redirect also fails.
- ✅ 3) Case B — welcome_seen:false → the welcome page IS shown, exactly once. Both roles. This counter-case is load-bearing: without it, a spec that simply never redirects would satisfy criterion 2 while the feature was entirely broken.
- ✅ 4) Case C — no flash. A framenavigated collector records every main-frame URL; the assertion is that the welcome route was never transiently visited. A URL-at-the-end check alone would miss a redirect that bounced back.
- ✅ 5) TEETH — proven, not assumed. Stubbed seedWelcomeSeenFromLogin to a no-op and rebuilt: exactly the two welcome_seen=true tests failed (at the not.toHaveURL line), and the two counter-cases correctly still passed. Restored → 4/4 green, and git diff frontend/src/ is empty so the revert was clean.
- ⏳ 6) CI 'E2E (Playwright smoke)' green on the PR — running at handoff; the job is gated on the frontend path filter, which this PR trips.
- ✅ Also: npx tsc --noEmit clean; eslint 0 errors.

## Decisions made
- Drove the REAL login form, not seedAuth(). The ticket flagged this and it is the crux: the seed runs on the login path only, so seedAuth() — which writes the auth keys directly and never calls setSession — would bypass the code under test entirely and model the pre-fix bug. The teeth check is what proves the spec actually exercises the seed.
- Non-email identifier + no email on the mocked user. useAuth only attempts the Supabase sign-in when response.user.email ?? (identifier contains '@') is truthy. Choosing e2e-hr / e2e-employee and omitting email makes that branch unreachable, so nothing calls the placeholder Supabase host. Confirmed #auth-login-identifier is type="text", so a non-email value is accepted by the form.
- Did not extend support/auth.ts or support/mockApi.ts. A login helper with a welcome_seen knob is used by exactly one spec; inlining it keeps the shared helpers untouched and the spec self-explanatory.
- Explicit 1s settle before the negative assertion. useWelcomeRedirect fires in a mount effect, so asserting the negative immediately would pass by looking too early — the settle is what makes "it did not redirect" mean something. Paired with the navigation collector so absence is proven two ways.
- Did not opt into trackConsoleErrors. It is opt-in in this harness, and the preview build's unmocked-asset 404s would add noise without testing anything this spec is about.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1674 (1 file, +~125). Confirm the CI E2E (Playwright smoke) check is green.
2. To re-prove the teeth yourself: stub seedWelcomeSeenFromLogin in frontend/src/utils/welcomeSeen.ts to a no-op, run cd frontend && npx playwright test welcome.persistence — the two welcome_seen=true tests must fail — then revert.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- The spec proves the CLIENT contract, not the server one. It asserts that a login response carrying welcome_seen:true suppresses the welcome page. It does not verify the backend actually sets welcome_seen from profiles.welcome_seen_at — that is covered by backend/tests/test_welcome_seen.py (AIQ-1701). The two halves meet only in production; nothing hermetic exercises the full round trip.
- Preview mode rebuilds the bundle per run, so a stale dist/ cannot mask a regression here. Worth remembering if anyone adds reuseExistingServer behaviour — a reused server WOULD serve a stale bundle and silently invalidate a teeth check.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.title: Investigate PageDown / stale-session force-logout on Services page
rows.notes:
## What was built
A written root cause. The answer is BOTH halves of the spec: the reported PageDown symptom is a harness artifact, AND a real single-session user is exposed via a different, slower path. No code changed — this was a Research task.

## Files changed
None — investigation only.

## Root cause

1. No keyboard path to logout exists. git grep -in "pagedown" over frontend/src/ returns ZERO hits. I enumerated every file with a keydown listener and checked which could log out: exactly one (frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx), and its handler responds only to Escape, only to close a menu — handleSignOut is a button click. It is also the ADMIN layout, not Services. PageDown is innocent; it scrolls.

2. The actual force-logout path: frontend/src/api/client.ts:4150 handle401Redirect(). On ANY 401 from the native-fetch helpers it calls clearAuthItems() (removing every relopass_* key) then window.location.href = '/auth?mode=login&reason=session_expired'. That IS "global logout, bounced to sign-in" — exactly the reported symptom.

3. What produces the 401: backend/app/auth_deps.py:108 raises 401 "Invalid token" when get_user_by_token() returns None. That happens when the token has no public.sessions row, OR when _session_is_expired(created_at) — backend/db/auth.py:32, SESSION_TTL_DAYS = 14, ABSOLUTE, no sliding refresh.

## The reported symptom: ARTIFACT — confirmed
Audos minted fixtures A and B in ONE browser. Login writes relopass_token to localStorage, so fixture B's login OVERWRITES fixture A's token. A still-mounted view holding fixture A's context 401s on its next fetch → handle401Redirect → global logout. PageDown merely scrolled, which preceded/triggered that next fetch, creating a false causal link.

I reproduced the MECHANISM incidentally today while verifying AIQ-1728: injecting an employee session then an HR session into the same browser overwrote relopass_token, and the pre-existing admin@relopass.com session died exactly this way. Same cause, no keyboard involved.

A real single-session user cannot hit this path — it requires a second login overwriting the first token in the same browser profile.

## BUT — a real exposure does exist (different, slower, not the reported bug)
The 14-day TTL is ABSOLUTE with no refresh. The code comment at backend/db/auth.py:31 calls a sliding/refresh mechanism "a documented follow-up". So a genuine single-session user who logged in 14 days ago gets force-logged-out on their NEXT API call — mid-flow, no warning, clearAuthItems() + a hard window.location.href that discards unsaved in-progress work.

Measured in prod: 7,203 session rows — 1,306 within TTL, 5,897 (82%) already past it.

Checked and ruled out: sessions.created_at is TEXT, and _session_is_expired treats an unparseable value as EXPIRED (fail-closed). Stored format is clean ISO (2026-02-19T00:33:56.411394) and parses correctly, so there is no accidental mass-expiry bug. Both sides compare naive UTC consistently.

## Validation results
- PASS Exact triggering code path identified: client.ts:4150 → auth_deps.py:108 → db/auth.py:35 (SESSION_TTL_DAYS = 14).
- PASS Single-session safety for the REPORTED symptom proven by construction: the only route to it is a second login overwriting relopass_token in the same browser.
- PASS The guardrail was respected — nothing disabled. The session-mismatch/expiry logout is a legitimate security control (SEC-FE-1) and remains intact.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Accept the artifact finding — no keyboard fix is warranted; the Audos report should not spawn a UI change.
2. Decide on the 14-day cliff separately (see gaps). It is pre-existing, not a regression, and NOT what Audos saw.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- No sliding session / refresh token. Already acknowledged in-code as a follow-up. Suggested task: "Sliding session refresh, or make the 401 landing non-destructive" — the cheaper half is preserving the current path and unsaved state across the forced redirect rather than discarding it.
- Not filed here: today measured 4 of 9 queue items as phantom work, so this should be searched against the queue before anyone opens it.

PREMISE: Refuted (PageDown→logout) · DUPLICATE: no · OUTCOME: docs

rows.title: Cannot reach server when requesting recommendations on services/questions page
rows.notes:
## What was built

The reported failure was NOT a connectivity failure. The request reached the server and returned 200 — it took 11,963 ms, and the axios client aborts at 12,000 ms, so it hung up 77 ms early and reported completed work as an unreachable server. Fixed on both sides: the batch call now carries a 60s timeout ceiling, and ~6.5s of post-answer telemetry moved off the response critical path.

PR: https://github.com/rlecomte1929/rolec/pull/1878 — branch fix/aiq-1856-recs-batch-timeout, commit 0b689d8c.

## Premise check (Phase 2.5) — REFUTED

Every lead on the ticket is false:
- CORS preflight — OPTIONS /api/recommendations/batch returns 200 with access-control-allow-origin: https://relopass.com.
- Backend down / route unregistered — POST returns 401 unauth, i.e. alive and registered.
- Proxy / base URL — production traffic reaches uvicorn (x-render-origin-server: uvicorn).

The failed-request telemetry on the report carries requestId=2d9ad2fe-613d-4064-9308-d96e8476b8aa. That exact request is in the Render log and it succeeded:


20:37:38.354  recommendations_batch succeeded dur_ms=4456.23
20:37:44.918  analytics event=recommendations_generated
20:37:45.056  status=200 elapsed_ms=11963


The client logged status: 0 at 20:37:44.980. The earlier attempt one minute before was the same request at elapsed_ms=12178.

The 6.5s gap between "answer ready" and "response sent" is the _log_slate loop, which re-runs the whole engine a second time per category (recommend_debug) purely to persist training rows.

## Files changed

- MODIFIED: frontend/src/features/recommendations/api.ts — explicit 60s timeout on recommendBatch (also covers the housing re-rank call in ServicesRecommendations.tsx)
- MODIFIED: backend/app/recommendations/router.py — the _log_slate loop dispatches via BackgroundTasks instead of running inline
- CREATED: frontend/src/features/recommendations/__tests__/recommendBatchTimeout.test.ts — pins the timeout above the 12s default
- CREATED: backend/tests/test_recommendations_batch_latency.py — pins that slate telemetry is scheduled, not awaited

## Validation results

- ✅ Both tests run RED against the unfixed code first — frontend fails with timeout undefined; backend fails with the slate writes already drained before the handler returns (0 != 2). The backend test calls the route function directly rather than via TestClient, which drains background tasks before returning.
- ✅ pytest backend/tests/test_recommendations_batch_latency.py backend/tests/test_services_case_scoping.py — 14 passed (re-run on a main-based branch)
- ✅ pytest backend/tests -k recommend — 58 passed
- ✅ vitest src/features/recommendations src/pages/services — 14 passed
- ✅ tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build clean
- ⚠️ Criteria 1–3 (button click succeeds, 2xx in DevTools, results render) need a post-deploy browser check — the fix is not live yet. Re-measured before implementing (plan step 1): Paris 46/46 rows unlinked, 79 approved-unlinked selections, 17 for this company across the three categories. Premise holds.

The warning's assertion — "likely a service_catalog_items external_id mismatch" — is false and has been removed. The two sides hold different vendors, so there was no id to link. search_by_service_destination requires platform_vetting_status='approved'; the FR registry housing_agencies rows are all pending, and the plugin is registry-only, so the engine produced ZERO candidates for that category.

- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/employee_recommendations_filter.py — surface approved masters the engine never ranked; _serves_destination + _canon_country gates; new hr_destination_gap status; the warning now states what was measured instead of guessing

- CREATED: backend/tests/test_employee_curation_catalog_masters.py — 11 tests

## Validation results

- ✅ Red-first proven: 8 of the 11 new tests FAIL against origin/main; the red run prints main's own misleading warning. The other 3 pin the degraded-read and HR-approved-nothing paths, which main already satisfies by design.
- ✅ Criteria 1–2 proven at the data level pre-deploy (read-only production query, approved / active / will-render-for-Paris / engine-resolvable-today): housing_agencies 4/4/4/0 · movers 4/4/4/0 · schools 9/9/9/0. 17 approved, 0 reachable today, 17 after this change.
- ✅ Criterion 3 (cross-tenant): covered by test_unapproved_master_never_surfaces + test_city_agnostic_selection_does_not_leak_another_citys_vendor — only ids in approved_master_ids reach the new path, and the destination gate stops a Madrid vendor rendering on a Paris case.

- Fixed in the filter, not the engine's candidate source. - Added a destination gate. Engine candidates were destination-scoped by the registry query; masters read straight from HR's approvals are not. Without it, a city-agnostic selection row pointing at a Madrid vendor would surface on a Paris case — a regression the fix would otherwise have introduced.

SECURITY: test-drive /provision invite-token gate is bypassable by omitting the token
rows.notes:
PAUSED — Red task with a live-campaign-breaking surprise; needs a product decision before any code.

FINDINGS (verified 2026-07-17):
1. The gate (test_drive.py:223-226) only 403s when a token is SUPPLIED-and-wrong; a MISSING token skips the check. So the abuse hole is real.
2. RELOPASS_TEST_DRIVE_INVITE_TOKEN IS set in prod (Render, len 23), and RELOPASS_TEST_DRIVE_ENABLED is on.
3. The live /test-drive campaign page sends NO token (links use ?campaign=, not ?token=). => Provisioning works today ONLY because of the missing-token bypass. If we 'fix' the gate to require a token when the env var is set, the LIVE CAMPAIGN 403s and breaks.

So there is no safe code-only fix. DECISION NEEDED:
(A) Public marketing test-drive (open by design): the token gate is vestigial/misconfigured. Fix = unset RELOPASS_TEST_DRIVE_INVITE_TOKEN (make 'gate off' explicit) and/or make the code+docstring honest; rely on the existing 5/min;60/hour rate-limit + is_test + autopurge for abuse. No campaign change. LOW risk.
(B) Invite-only provisioning: fix the gate to require a token when the env var is set, AND update the frontend + every campaign link to carry ?token=<secret>. Note: putting the secret in shareable URLs is itself a leak/privacy concern (URLs get logged/shared). MEDIUM risk + changes campaign distribution.

Recommendation: (A) — the test-drive is a public campaign; requiring per-link tokens fights its purpose and leaks the secret in URLs. If Romain wants real abuse protection, prefer a CAPTCHA / proof-of-work over URL tokens (separate task).

Original task premise ('just require the token') was based on not knowing the frontend sends none + the var is set. Corrected here.

rows.title: Recommendations: apply HR curation BEFORE the top_n slice — 74 of 78 companies render fewer approved suppliers than they have
rows.notes:
## What was built
HR curation now runs over the FULL ranked candidate list and the top_n slice runs afterwards, so a supplier HR approved that ranks below the cut is no longer discarded before the allowlist is consulted. The master resolution was batched first so the hot path is never O(candidates) queries.

PR #1667, branch fix/aiq-1700-curate-before-top-n, commit 81e8c0bd.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/service_catalog.py — new find_masters_by_supplier_or_external_ids(category, item_ids): batched sibling of the single-id resolver, same matching rule and the same external_id-wins tiebreak.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/employee_recommendations_filter.py — apply_hr_curation resolves masters through one batched call instead of one query per item. No semantic change.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/recommendations/engine.py — recommend() builds items for the full matching list when curation will run, curates, then applies top_n via the new _cap_masters_keep_customs. Un-curated path (company_id=None, advisory categories) slices exactly as before.
- CREATED: backend/tests/test_recommendations_curate_before_cut.py — 7 tests, one per validation criterion.

## The reproduction changed the plan — the naive fix has a defect
The ticket's HYPOTHESIS said to test the ordering interaction before assuming. Doing so found that "curate then slice" truncates HR's custom vendors. Customs are appended after the masters, and because the slice used to run before curation they were never subject to it: a company with 10 approved masters + 2 customs legitimately received 12 items. A plain items[:top_n] silently drops vendors HR added by hand. Hence _cap_masters_keep_customs — cap the masters, keep every custom.

## Validation results (measured on real prod inputs; only DB access stubbed)
- ✅ 1) Below-top_n approved supplier renders. Company approving 3 of 12 (2 ranked 11th/12th): 1 → 3 rendered, with 9 slots that had been sitting free. test_approved_supplier_ranked_below_top_n_still_renders.
- ✅ 2) top_n still caps. All-12 company still renders exactly 10. test_top_n_still_caps_the_master_picks.
- ✅ 3) hr_pending unchanged. Zero approvals + zero customs → ([], 'hr_pending') and record_demand still fires. test_hr_pending_still_fires_on_zero_approvals.
- ✅ 4) AIQ-1530 preserved. HR display_order still outranks engine score. test_display_order_still_wins_over_engine_rank.
- ✅ 5) Custom vendors not truncated. 12 approved + 2 customs, top_n=10 → 12 items, customs last — matching pre-change behaviour. test_custom_vendors_are_not_truncated_by_the_slice.
- ✅ 6) O(1) master-resolution queries. Measured on the reproduction: 10 → 1. test_master_resolution_is_batched asserts the batched helper is called once and the per-item helper never.
- ✅ 7) NL_SG regression. All-12 companies still render 10 movers, hr_curation_status None.
- ✅ 8) Test Command pytest -k "recommendation or movers or curation or catalog" → 145 passed, 6 skipped. Full suite → 5613 passed (14 failures = the documented pre-existing llm_client asyncio baseline). The 13 existing curation tests — including AIQ-1688 supplier_id resolution and AIQ-1690 twin dedup — pass unchanged against the batched resolver.
- ✅ Constraint: verified on real Postgres. The batched SQL was run read-only against prod (nsvefcvpvwwwhuqyuqmp): one query resolves all 12 movers masters; an unknown id returns nothing.

## Teeth (both proven, not assumed)
- Reverting only the engine ordering → test_approved_supplier_ranked_below_top_n_still_renders FAILS.
- Substituting a naive items[:top_n] → test_custom_vendors_are_not_truncated_by_the_slice FAILS (assert 10 == 12).
- Honest note: six of the seven new tests pass before and after — they are preservation guards, which is their job. Only the one encoding the actual bug fails pre-fix.

## Decisions made
- Batched the resolver as a separate first step, before touching the ordering, so the hot path is never briefly O(candidates) queries at any commit.
- _cap_masters_keep_customs lives in engine.py, not the filter — top_n is the engine's parameter and the filter has no business knowing about it.
- Building RecommendationItems for the full list is CPU-only. build_explanation is pure dict work with no I/O, so the extra objects cost no queries; the query cost was the real risk and it is now O(1).
- will_curate computed once and reused for both the slice decision and the curation branch, so the two can never disagree about whether curation is happening.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1667 (4 files, +300/−3). The behaviour-bearing lines are will_curate / top = matching if will_curate else matching[:top_n] and _cap_masters_keep_customs.
2. After merge + deploy, open a case for a company that approves a SUBSET of a category's suppliers and confirm more providers now render.
3. Spot-check a company with HR custom vendors and confirm the customs still appear after the masters.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- Result-set size grows for ~74 companies. That is the intent, but it is a visible product change: employees will see more providers than yesterday.
- The two SG suppliers with no supplier_scoring_metadata rating and no service_areas (SIRVA, Delahaye) rank last purely from missing data. They now surface for companies that approved them — correct, but the underlying registry data quality is worth its own look.
- _cap_masters_keep_customs means the endpoint can return more than top_n when HR has customs. That is pre-existing behaviour deliberately preserved, not new — flagging it because it can surprise a client that assumes len(recommendations) <= top_n.

rows.title: [AIQ-1737·3] Surgical repair of the 51 bad canonical_case_id rows (author + operator-apply)

## What was done
Surgical repair of the canonical_case_id stock, executed out-of-band via execute_sql (operator-approved by Romain). prod public.case_assignments is now 1:1-clean: 0 null / 0 dangling / 0 duplicate (verified post-write).

## Method (collision-safe unified rule)
Ranked every assignment by effective canonical = COALESCE(canonical_case_id, case_id); kept ONE survivor per effective-canonical group (preferring a row that already has a valid canonical, then earliest); deleted the rest + all orphans; set the 2 clean-null survivors' canonical = case_id. Children deleted by assignment_id only, so kept siblings sharing a case_id were untouched. One atomic transaction, guarded by a DO-block that aborts if the plan size drifts from the validated 42 delete / 2 update.

## Bug caught before writing
The naive per-class plan would have set 3 demo-ca-00X null rows to canonical=case_id — colliding with their duplicate-group survivors (5b16522e / 1cbc563e / 65d7aea8) and RE-creating duplicates. The unified rule folds them in as duplicate-extras instead. Caught via the read-only capture; corrected before any write.

## Numbers
- DELETE 42 assignments (23 duplicate-extras + 19 orphans) + 48 child rows (assignment_mobility_links 20, case_events 24, assignment_claim_invites 2, legacy_employee_profiles 2; case_evidence/case_feedback/relocation_tasks 0 — all 7 FK children of case_assignments covered).
- UPDATE 2 null rows → canonical=case_id (51a4761f employee_test, af4bbb3f employee@may.com).
- 7 duplicate-survivors auto-fixed (became unique once siblings removed). 42 + 2 + 7 = 51 bad rows resolved.

- ✅ Post-write: total_bad = 0 (null 0 / dangling 0 / duplicate 0); total_assignments 481.
- ✅ Affected-row count == bad-row count exactly (42 del + 2 upd + 7 sibling-fixed = 51); the DO-block guard enforced 42/2 or would have aborted the tx.
- ✅ No legitimate/clean row altered — children deleted by assignment_id; kept siblings untouched.

rows.title: Fix 400 error blocking supplier submission approval on /admin/supplier-submissions
rows.notes:
## Resolved by PR #1601 (another agent) — my overlapping PR #1602 closed as redundant

Core bug FIXED by #1601 (b202d611, merged 2026-07-21): supplier submissions are now validated at SUBMIT time in hr_supplier_submissions.create() (calls validate_capability), so an unapprovable row (e.g. coverage_scope_type='country' with no country_code) can no longer be created → the admin approval 400 can't recur for new submissions.

Root cause (confirmed in repo): validate_capability (run inside create_supplier at approval) requires a 2-letter country_code when scope is 'country'/'city' (supplier_validation.py:76-84). The HR form set scope='country' whenever no city was given — even with no country — and the submit path stored it unvalidated. So the row could be created but never approved (PATCH .../supplier-submissions/{id} approve → ValueError → 400 at admin_catalog.py:650). (The [id]-interpolation lead was disproven; the payload shape {action,notes} matches ResolveSubmissionBody.)

Prod state (verified via SQL): 3 pending submissions, 0 stuck/unapprovable (no country-less country/city rows). So no legacy rows remain for an approve()-side fix to unblock — my #1602 (which fixed approve() to derive scope + a frontend change) was redundant on the merged #1601 and is CLOSED.

## Known follow-up (small, NOT yet shipped — needs a product call)
With #1601's submit-time validation live, the HR form (frontend/src/pages/HrPreferredSupplierCard.tsx:57) still sends coverage_scope_type: city ? 'city' : 'country' — i.e. 'country' even when NO country is entered (the country field is optional in the form). So a legitimate country-less preferred-supplier submission now 400s at submit with a cryptic 'country_code required' message — a minor UX regression from #1601. Two clean fixes: (a) derive scope client-side ('global' when no country), or (b) make the country field required in the form. Recommend (a) if a country-less 'global' preferred supplier is allowed; (b) if country is mandatory. Left for a product decision rather than an overlapping PR.

## Reviewer
1. Verify on /admin/supplier-submissions that approving a normal (country/city) submission works (it does — #1601).
2. Decide the country-less HR-submit follow-up (allow-as-global vs require-country).

rows.title: Trigger engine: _derive_events reads origin from the draft only, so roadmap.profile_completed never fires for a case at rest
rows.notes:
## What was built
PR #1750. _derive_events now reads origin from the already-resolved context instead of recomputing it from derived/basics, so it agrees with _build_context.

## The premise as filed is REFUTED — read this first
The task claimed roadmap.profile_completed NEVER fires for a case at rest. Checked against prod before writing code: 141 at-rest cases have a spouse dependent and 139 already carry the spouse form. It does fire — the FIRST PATCH carries relocationBasics. Of the 2 apparent misses, one (214214b4) has AE-FAM-SPOUSE (a template code my query didn't cover) and the other (bf172747) stores 'India'/'Germany' as country NAMES — that is the separate normalisation task, not this one.

The estimated blast radius in this task (~217 cases) was therefore also wrong. Measured properly: the eligibility query returns an EMPTY set. Zero new attachments.

## The narrower defect that IS real
The wizard does not persist relocationBasics into cases.intake_data (verified live). So a SECOND PATCH — later step or HR edit — carries no originCountry. On it, destination_confirmed fires (dest resolves from the DB) but profile_completed does not. A dependent added between the two PATCHes never gets its form.

Red test before the fix: AssertionError: 'UTL-2011F' not found in ['GP-7-04']. GP-7-04 is destination-only and attached; UTL-2011F needs profile_completed and did not.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/trigger_engine.py — _derive_events reads context['origin_country']; dropped the now-unused basics local.
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_trigger_engine.py — added the red-first regression test and a contract test; corrected a helper test whose hand-built context was a state _build_context cannot produce.

rows.title: Task generator asserts unverified root causes as fact — 4 false-premise tasks in one day
rows.notes:
## What was built
The feedback→task generator can no longer assert a root cause it has no evidence for, and the pipeline no longer hands it noise labelled as evidence. Enforcement is deterministic (a new scorer dimension), not just prose in the prompt — and the nightly path is gated for the first time.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/feedback_task_engineer.py — _SYSTEM contract; format_diagnostics (breadcrumbs/route through, buffer labelled, _FAILED_REQUEST_LIMIT); extract_confirmed_signals (has_confirmed_cause split out); score_task (D3 reframed, D6 added); _asserted_causes + _ASSERTED_CAUSE_RE; leads_unverified key folded into execution_prompt.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/autopilot_ingest.py — eval gate before create_work_queue_task; truncation aligned to the shared constant.
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_feedback_task_score.py — 12 regression tests replaying the two real reports.

## Validation results
- ✅ Replaying BUG-260716-D23E: /api/admin/exec-overview (4th in the buffer) is no longer truncated away; the buffer is labelled unfiltered/session-wide/lead; has_confirmed_cause is False for buffer-only evidence; D6 blocks AIQ-1564's actual text.
- ✅ Replaying BUG-260717-3D77: breadcrumbs reach the prompt (/admin/outreach present); route labelled "not necessarily the page being described".
- ✅ No silent truncation — showing 5 of 9 asserted; one _FAILED_REQUEST_LIMIT replaces three disagreeing slices.
- ✅ D6 penalises an asserted cause without a frame; omitting a buffered endpoint is no longer penalised.
- ✅ autopilot_ingest._dispatch_one() runs the gate before dispatch and skips on failure.
- ✅ Existing suites intact: test_feedback_task_score 32 passed, test_feedback_task_engineer_parse, test_notion_work_queue_properties, test_dispatch_notion, test_feedback_diagnostics_enrichment, test_autonomy_tier — 289 passed across the feedback/autopilot/notion/dispatch selection.
- ✅ No regression in useful output — a confirmed failingFrame still yields a task that references it (D2 untouched); a frame still licenses a stated cause.
- ⚠️ F6 (decomposition author) NOT done — see Known gaps. This is why the result is Partial, not Passed.

## Decisions made
- Enforcement lives in score_task, not the prompt. An anti-speculation rule is prose an LLM may ignore; D6 is deterministic and testable. This mirrors the existing belt-and-suspenders post-processing that already auto-corrects question-like text to Research.
- Leads kept, not banned. The 429s in AIQ-1564 were real; the modals in AIQ-1566 were genuinely cropped. Silencing the model would trade one failure for another, so theories live in leads_unverified as questions.
- leads_unverified folded into execution_prompt rather than added as a Notion property — the property map is 1:1 from LLM keys, so an unmapped key is dropped silently, and adding a DB property is out of scope. The heading is what makes it non-binding.
- _ASSERTED_CAUSE_RE is deliberately narrow. Bare "because"/"so that" are excluded — they carry no mechanism claim. Validated against real text: catches 1564, silent on 1565/1566/innocent-because/symptom-only.
- D6 fires only when there is no failingFrame AND the task is impl-typed AND status is Ready for AI — so a false positive costs a re-type to Research, never a lost fix.
- Found and fixed a real bug in my own patch: autopilot_ingest's module logger is log, not logger — logger.warning would have NameError'd in the nightly path where nobody is watching.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1510.
2. cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_feedback_task_score.py -q — expect 32 passed.
3. The honest end-to-end test is a live one: dispatch a real feedback item from /admin/feedback and read the drafted spec. It should state the symptom, name no cause, and put any theory under "Leads — UNVERIFIED".

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- F6 not done. AIQ-1556's false premise ("Email REQUIRED by default") came from a plan-doc decomposition, not this generator. The ticket said "identify the author first — do not assume a file". I did not identify it, so I did not touch it. Naming a file I hadn't verified would be the exact error this ticket exists to stop. Worth a follow-up: find the decomposition author and apply the same rule.
- test_feedback_pipeline_gaps.py (live-LLM, skipped without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) is where an end-to-end replay belongs. The deterministic half is covered offline in test_feedback_task_score.py; the live half is not written.
- The D6 regex is a heuristic. It catches the phrasings that actually shipped; a novel phrasing could slip through. The prompt contract is the first net, D6 the second — neither is complete alone.

### Validation results (all 4 criteria)
1. PASS (with one intentional exception, see below) — France->Norway output deep-equal to the pre-change snapshot. Snapshots captured against the PROVABLY unmodified engine before any edit; after the entire change their ONLY diff is the additive "anchorKind" field (x6). Every requirement, offset, feasibility, count and banner value byte-identical.
2. PASS — ES_IE inside the runway returns a red critical banner; outside it returns none. Boundary tested both sides.
3. PASS — every ES_IE employment-permit requirement reports owner 'HR'. The visa application is correctly left with the Employee (it is genuinely theirs to file).
4. PASS — the 42 literal is gone. Both corridors derive their threshold from their own offsets via derivedRunwayDays(): FR->NO 112d, ES_IE 126d.

Suite: 24 passed (11 FR->NO incl. 6 snapshots, 13 ES_IE).

### ⚠️ DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — Romain approved 2026-08-04
Criteria 1 and 4 CONFLICTED: criterion 4 demanded the 42 literal go, criterion 1 demanded no FR->NO behaviour change, and deriving FR->NO's threshold gives 112 not 42. Romain chose 'derive both, accept the FR->NO change'.

Effect: FR->NO's banner now fires from 112 days out instead of 42. Justified on the merits too — the old 6-week figure was SHORTER than the corridor's own longest-lead step (UDI work permit at T-16 weeks), so the banner could stay silent while that step was already unachievable.

CRITICAL DETAIL: none of the six pre-existing snapshot fixtures falls in the 42-112 day band, so re-capturing alone would have shown no diff and looked like 'no behaviour change' when the rule genuinely changed. Added an explicit test at 59 days out plus both boundary cases to pin it.

### Design problem found and fixed mid-implementation
Deriving the threshold forced the question of what 'runway' means per anchor kind, and the two run in OPPOSITE directions:
  move-date       -> time UNTIL the move (work precedes the anchor)
  contract-signed -> time ELAPSED SINCE signature (the chain runs forward from it)
My first draft measured ES_IE against 'time until', which is backwards — it made a contract signed further in the FUTURE look safer. Corrected: a future signature now correctly warns (nothing in the chain has started). The tests encode the corrected direction explicitly.

### Compatibility
Exported type names unchanged (CorridorCheck.tsx and case-obligations.ts import them); runCaseCheck stays pure with today injected; corridorId defaults to 'france-norway' so every existing call site is untouched.

### Follow-up needed (own ticket)

rows.title: S1 · Declare an explicit arrival_anchor step in the corridor pathway schema
rows.notes:
## Done — PR #1710 (branch feat/aiq-1747-arrival-anchor, commit a1a67629)

### What was built
Added arrival_anchor: bool = False to CorridorStep in backend/relopass/corridors/loader.py, coerced from YAML alongside the existing non_obvious / outcome_type flags, and marked exactly one step in each of the 10 pathway files.

### The two judgement calls (both resolved by reading the graph, not guessing)
- NO_FR -> A0_DEPART_NO. The corridor has NO 'arrive in France' step at all, because a returning EEA citizen needs no visa, permit or registration (C2_IMMIGRATION_RIGHT_OF_RETURN). Departure IS the move event; runway legitimately 0.
- IN_DE -> TRAVEL_TO_DE, but the graph roots at ZAB_STATEMENT, not travel.
A TRAVEL_TO_* prefix match would have mis-anchored both — which is exactly why the field was declared rather than inferred.

### Measured result (the evidence for the whole AIQ-1745 design)
Pre-arrival lead time once anchored:
  IN_DE  TRAVEL_TO_DE  158 days
  ES_IE  TRAVEL_TO_IE  104 days   <- matches the hand-calc in the parent brief
  DE_NO/ES_NL/FR_CH/FR_DE/FR_ES/FR_NL/FR_NO  1 day
  NO_FR  A0_DEPART_NO  0 days
Permit vs free-movement separates by two orders of magnitude from the step graph alone. Confirms S2 needs no corridor allowlist, and IN_DE (Blue Card) inherits the downstream feature for free — a bonus the parent brief did not anticipate.

### Validation results
- Criterion 1 PASS — exactly one arrival_anchor per pathway across all 10 (test_every_pathway_declares_exactly_one_anchor).
- Criterion 2 PASS — unmarked steps default to False; absent key still loads (test_unmarked_steps_default_to_false).
- Criterion 3 PASS — no regressions. Full corridor suite: 102 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failures (test_corridor_pathways / step_flags / registry / sla / in_de_bluecard_2026 / no_fr / responsibility / persistence).
- Extra: added test_anchor_is_the_semantically_correct_step so a future corridor cannot land with a merely-present anchor.

### Safety
Purely additive. No step_id renamed — corridor_persistence.py derives rce.steps ids via uuid5(_NS, f'step:{corridor_id}:{step_key}'), so a rename would silently orphan persisted rows.

### Environment note for the next executor
Local python is 3.9; the repo needs 3.11. Ran via: uv run --python 3.11 --with pytest --with pyyaml --with sqlalchemy --with psycopg2-binary python -m pytest ...  (sqlalchemy is required to collect test_corridor_registry.py and test_corridor_persistence.py — without it they ERROR on import, which is environmental and not a code failure.)

### What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1710; confirm CI green.
2. Sanity-check the two non-obvious anchors (NO_FR = A0_DEPART_NO, IN_DE = TRAVEL_TO_DE) against the corridor content — these are the only real judgement calls in the change.
3. Merge; S2 (AIQ-1748) unblocks immediately.

rows.title: TD-QA R2-09 · Password field carries autofill residue between persona logins (HR <-> Employee)
TD-BUG-1 · HR 'Add your first relocation' CTA is a dead-end loop — never opens a case form
rows.notes:
## What was built
The HR command-center's primary CTA now opens the real case-creation form instead of silently bouncing to the onboarding wizard. Plus a static guard so a navigate() to a non-existent route fails CI rather than shipping as an invisible dead-end.

## Root cause — NOT the guard the task hedged at
The task guessed "likely an onboarding-incomplete guard firing" (properly hedged — and not what it was).

Both buttons called navigate('/employees/new'). There is no such route.


'Add your first relocation' → navigate('/employees/new')     ← no matching <Route>
  → <Route path="*"> → NotFoundRedirect → roleHomePath('HR') = /hr/dashboard
     → useWelcomeRedirect('/hr/welcome') → hasSeenWelcome() false → /hr/welcome


Every hop of the reported trace, explained. It repeated 3x because hasSeenWelcome() only flips on skip/CTA — which the tester never reached. Nothing failed loudly: a dead path is invisible to tsc (it's a string) and invisible at runtime (the catch-all swallows it).

The tell was next door — the sibling actions use buildRoute('hrEmployees') / buildRoute('hrPolicy'); only these two used a hand-written string never added to ROUTE_DEFS.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/features/platform-v2/mobility-control/MobilityControlCenterV2Page.tsx — both dead-route buttons now use buildRoute; the CTA opens the form via ?new=1.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/pages/HrDashboard.tsx — honours ?new=1 → openNewCaseForm(), consuming the param on mount.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/hooks/useWelcomeRedirect.ts — new optional { skip }.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/hooks/useWelcomeRedirect.test.tsx — 2 new cases.
- CREATED: frontend/src/navigation/navigateTargets.test.ts — systemic guard.

## Validation results
- ✅ Test Command cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit — exit 0.
- ✅ CTA no longer bounces to /hr/welcome — the dead route is gone; the guard proves no literal navigate() target is unroutable.
- ✅ Only one canonical form — both entry points now converge on HrDashboard's openNewCaseForm, the form the task said to keep. No second form introduced.
- ✅ Fresh test-drive HR — { skip } stops a first-run welcome hijacking the CTA; unit-covered both ways (skips with intent, still redirects without).
- ✅ No regression — frontend 1619 passed / 226 files; eslint clean on the changed files.
- ✅ Guard proven by negative test — reintroducing navigate('/employees/new') fails it, naming the exact file and call; passes once fixed.
- ⚠️ "case created + assigned end-to-end from that path" — needs a live browser run post-deploy. The routing and the form-open are unit-covered; the full create+assign flow is not reachable from jsdom.

## Decisions made
- ?new=1 rather than a new route. The form is local state (setFormOpen), so a caller cannot route to it directly. A query param is the seam, and it matches the file's existing ?status= / ?destination= convention. A new route would have meant a second form — the exact duplication the task asked to end.
- { skip } on the welcome hook, not deleting the redirect. PR #1507's first-login welcome is intended behaviour. The bug is that it overrode a deliberate destination — so an explicit intent wins, and a plain first login is untouched.
- The guard reads both route sources. ROUTE_DEFS alone flags /journey and /dashboard as dead when they are real literal routes in App.tsx — a guard that cries wolf gets deleted, so it had to be right on the first run.
- Swept all 7 hardcoded navigate() targets — /employees/new was the only dead one. No other CTA of this class is broken before the cohort link goes out.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1511.
2. Post-deploy, on a fresh test-drive HR account: from /hr/command-center click "Add your first relocation" → expect the case form to open on the Cases page, not /hr/welcome. Then create + assign a case end-to-end (the ⚠️ above).
3. Click "Manage cases" → expect the Cases page.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- The end-to-end create+assign path is not automated — it needs the live browser check in step 2.
- The guard covers only literal navigate('/…') calls. Template literals and buildRoute() are dynamic or already type-checked; a computed dead path could still slip through. Narrow on purpose — the noisy version gets deleted.
- TD-BUG-4 (AIQ-1571, "HR onboarding buries case creation") pairs with this and is still open; it addresses the wider funnel, not the dead route.
