rows.title: TD-BUG-3 · Verify + fix the AUTOMATED over-cap → policy-exception → HR notification path
rows.notes:
## Correction first: my earlier 'Blocked' note was wrong

The previous Execution Notes claimed the automated guardrail 'does not exist at any layer', that 'the employee's selection carries no price', and that 'nothing compares a price to a cap' — concluding there was no trigger point and a product decision was required. Re-verified against the code AND live prod on 2026-07-17: all three claims are false. The note asserted a conclusion from an incomplete search (it missed the entire exception_requests router and the estimate page). Superseded in full by the findings below.

## What is actually true

1. The trigger exists and is employee-facing. /employee/case/:caseId/services/estimate → PackageSummary.tsx renders each vendor's price (metadata.estimated_cost_usd) next to the policy cap (from GET /api/cases/{id}/budget-summary), computes status: 'over' | 'within' | 'not_capped' (:236-245), and shows a 'Request exception' CTA to employees only when over (:603-619).
2. The exception request already worked — proven by live prod data, not a unit test. POST /api/cases/{case_id}/exception-requests (exception_requests.py:320) → INSERT INTO policy_cap_requests; registered in both apps (main.py:849, app/main.py:201). Prod holds a real row: housing, 32,000 NOK requested vs a 25,000 NOK cap, exception_type='cap_override', status approved.
3. Two cap evaluators exist (policy_config_cap_compare.py:282, policy_engine.py:183).
4. The one real gap: create_exception_request wrote the row + an audit log and notified nobody. The prod row above was approved by an HR user who was never told.

## What was built

The assigned HR now gets an in-app notification (POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUESTED) naming the category and requested-vs-cap amounts, deep-linked to /hr/exceptions — the inbox that has the approve/reject flow — rather than the default employee-dashboard target. Reuses the canonical pattern at routers/cases_write.py:296-319; wrapped so a notification failure can never fail the employee's request. No new table, no migration, no Resend (per the task's constraint).

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/routers/exception_requests.py — _notify_hr_of_exception_request() + call site in create_exception_request
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_exception_requests_router.py — 6 new tests
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/constants/notificationTypes.ts — new type + /hr/exceptions deep-link
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/pages/NotificationSettings.tsx — HR toggle for the new type

## Decisions made
- Kept employee-initiated rather than fully auto-filing (Romain's call). The system detects over-cap and offers the CTA; the employee files with a reason. Auto-filing would open exceptions merely for browsing an expensive vendor, and would reach HR with no justification — the field they need to decide. This still satisfies the criteria: over-cap → exception + HR notified; under-cap → nothing (the CTA only renders when status === 'over').
- Recipient resolution verified against prod, not assumed: policy_cap_requests.case_id matches case_assignments.case_id, not .id. So get_assignment_by_case_id is correct.
- _is_sqlite_engine() reads the dialect off the live engine rather than a module-level DATABASE_URL snapshot, because the tests swap db.engine for in-memory SQLite — a snapshot would report Postgres while the code talks to SQLite.

## Validation results
- ✅ pytest backend/tests/test_exception_requests_router.py → 23 passed (6 new)
- ✅ pytest backend/tests/ -k "exception or notification" → 135 passed (verified in a clean worktree and with DATABASE_URL pinned to sqlite)
- ✅ npx tsc --noEmit → No errors found
- ⚠️ Driven end-to-end run NOT yet done — the task explicitly demands 'a real driven flow, not a unit assumption'. See reviewer steps; this is the one criterion still outstanding.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- 27 of 239 prod assignments can never receive this notification. notifications.user_id is uuid NOT NULL while users.id is text; those assignments carry a legacy non-uuid hr_user_id (the seed-* demo accounts) so the INSERT fails the uuid cast. They are skipped with a greppable HR NOT NOTIFIED WARNING rather than silently dropped. Resolving to the Supabase auth uuid would not help — the bell reads by ReloPass users.id, so the row would be written and unreadable. Test-drive HR accounts are minted uuid.uuid4() (test_drive.py:194), so the wave is unaffected.
- This also corrects an in-repo claim (roadmap_review_notification.py:10-15) that in-app notifications are dead — that generalises from one seed account; 678/679 HR users are uuid-castable.
- AIQ-1587 (P0) filed from this work: prod's policy_exceptions runs the redesign shape while db/policies.py queries the legacy one → 4 HR endpoints 500. Deliberately not bundled here.
- Three 'policy exception' tables exist: policy_cap_requests (employee writes → HR inbox reads — works), exception_requests (what the HR case panel reads — different vocabulary: cost_threshold/tenure_insufficient), policy_exceptions (dead). So the case-summary panel will not show an employee's cap-override request. Flagged in AIQ-1587; merging the three is a product-model decision.
- Unrelated local hazard spotted: test_p3_exception_wiring.py:42 uses os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite://…"), which cannot override a local .env — so that unit test connects to production on a dev machine. Reproduced on unmodified main; CI has no .env so it never fires there. Worth hardening.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1520.
2. Drive the real flow (the outstanding criterion): as a test-drive employee, shortlist an over-cap vendor on /employee/case/:caseId/services/estimate, click 'Request exception', submit — then confirm the assigned HR's bell shows 'Policy exception requested' and it links to /hr/exceptions.

rows.title: Wire EN/NO translation into the dossier form flow (labels only, values verbatim)
rows.notes:
## ⚠️ MY REFUTATION IS NOW SUPERSEDED — corrected 2026-08-04, later the same day

This task WAS correctly refuted, and is now correctly DONE. Both are true, in that order, and the reason is worth recording.

### What I said, and why it was right at the time
I refuted this task because its trigger condition is form_templates.source_language != 'en', and ALL 83 templates in prod were 'en'. The feature would have been unreachable code on the day it shipped. That was accurate when measured.

### What changed — my own action invalidated my own finding
Later that day I applied the never-applied seed migration 20261015000000, which inserts RP-NO-DATASHEET with source_language = 'nb'. Prod is now:

    en: 83 templates
    nb:  1 template   <- RP-NO-DATASHEET

So the condition source_language != 'en' now matches exactly one template — the FR->NO data-sheet this whole slice exists to serve. The premise became true because I made it true.

### The work shipped, and it is better than the task asked for
PR #1731 (commit e0f431f2) is merged to main. Its approach: labels render through /api/translate (domain='ui', cached) with the seeded label_nb as an authoritative instant override, degrading to the original label on 503. Identifier VALUES are never translated and never sent to the service. form_templates.source_language is surfaced on the form summary.

That is precisely the design my refutation recommended as the useful version of this task ("make the toggle fall back to the translation service when label_nb is absent") — label_nb wins when present, translation fills the gap otherwise. It does not stack dead code on dead code, which was my objection.

### Lesson worth keeping
A refutation is a measurement, not a permanent verdict. This one was correct against the data as it stood and was overturned within hours by a data change — made by me, in the same session, for a different task. Re-measure before treating a recorded refutation as settled.

### Still unverified
That the toggle RENDERS in the running UI and that toggling leaves values byte-identical. That needs a case with the data-sheet attached; currently zero cases have it (the trigger fix in PR #1742 makes it possible, but nothing has fired roadmap.destination_confirmed yet).

## Outcome: DUPLICATE — superseded mid-execution. No code shipped.

The dedupe precheck (Phase 1c) was clean when this started; the duplicate landed while it was in flight. Two sessions covered the whole scope:

- AIQ-1726 / PR #1682 — services_state canonical-id fix + guard coverage.
- AIQ-1719 / PR #1684 — resolved the 8 forms/dossier reads and cleared the guard allowlist.

My PR #1681 was closed, not merged. Branch deleted.

## The premise was real — and the ticket had it backwards

This ticket (which I authored) claimed "AIQ-1707 has since migrated the endpoints; this task only extends the GUARD." That was wrong. Phase 2.5 proved no AIQ-1704 commit had ever touched services_state.py (last change: AIQ-1320). Both endpoints still bound the raw path param, so the phantom-write hole — the worst instance in the epic — was live on main at the time. The guard extension turned red immediately, which is exactly what a guard is for.

## Their fix is better than mine — recorded so the reasoning isn't lost

I resolved with db.resolve_case_ids(case_id), costing an extra DB round-trip. They reuse the assignment row require_case_access already returned:

python
case_id = str((assignment or {}).get("canonical_case_id") or (assignment or {}).get("case_id") or case_id)


Identical semantics — including the or case_id passthrough — at zero extra query cost. Their guard also added a _resolves() helper that recognises this require_case_access + canonical_case_id pattern, so it isn't mistaken for an unresolved endpoint.

## Production-data findings (the part worth keeping)

Verified read-only against prod while validating the fix shape. Not recorded anywhere else:

rows.title: [E2E-Sentinel] confirm-twice must fail closed when REOPENING a Done task (+ robust $prev resolution)
rows.notes:
## What was built
Reopening a human-closed (terminal) task is now fail-CLOSED: the E2E Sentinel reopens a Done/Rejected/Archived task only when the failure is CONFIRMED (also failed the previous run). An unconfirmed/first-seen flap is HELD, not resurrected — fixing the AIQ-1375 deploy-window recurrence. New-task CREATE keeps today's fail-open. PR #1695, branch fix/aiq1738-confirm-twice-reopen-failclosed, commit 7533971d.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: scripts/notion_sync_candidates.py — terminal_action() gains a confirmed arg (default True → legacy 2-arg callers unchanged) + a new hold outcome for terminal+non-GREEN+not-confirmed; main() computes confirmed = (not confirm_twice_active) or (test_id in prev_ids) per candidate, holds the reopen when unconfirmed, and surfaces a held-reopen count. CREATE/note stay fail-open.
- MODIFIED: .github/workflows/e2e-campaign.yml — resolve $prev by walking recent COMPLETED runs and taking the first with a downloadable sentinel-state artifact (near-simultaneous runs raced the old [0] pick → 'no previous run found' → fail-open).
- MODIFIED: scripts/tests/test_notion_sync_passing_guard.py — reopen-fail-closed cases (hold on unconfirmed; reopen on confirmed; GREEN wins; open=note-only; the exact AIQ-1375 shape; legacy 2-arg default).
- MODIFIED: scripts/tests/test_notion_confirm_twice.py — interaction test: no baseline → CREATE fails open but REOPEN fails closed.

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) terminal + non-GREEN + NOT confirmed → held (AMBER/RED/INCONCLUSIVE/None/''/'N/A').
- ✅ 2) terminal + non-GREEN + confirmed → reopen.
- ✅ 3) terminal + GREEN → skip; open task → note-only (AIQ-1625 preserved).
- ✅ 4) NEW candidate + no prev state → still created (fail-open preserved).
- ✅ 5) $prev walks completed runs for a downloadable sentinel-state artifact — YAML parses + actionlint clean; bash uses only RUN_ID (github.run_id) + GH-API databaseIds (no untrusted input).
- ✅ 6) .venv311/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/ -q → 87 passed.

## Decisions made
- confirmed defaults True so callers that don't use confirm-twice (manual/legacy) keep reopen-on-any-non-GREEN; only the workflow path (which always passes --confirm-twice) gets fail-closed reopen.
- Kept terminal_action tests in their existing home (test_notion_sync_passing_guard.py) + an interaction test in the confirm-twice file.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- Trade-off: a genuine regression on a closed task now needs 2 runs (+ working prev-state) to reopen — acceptable; the $prev hardening keeps confirmation reliable. New-bug detection unchanged.

rows.title: TD-BUG-2 · 'Sign in' assumes a logged-out visitor — already-authenticated users land in the wrong account
rows.notes:
## What was built
The /test-drive credentials block no longer assumes a logged-out visitor. With a live session it names the account you're actually in and offers one-click sign-out, instead of silently dropping you back into your own account.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/pages/public/TestDrivePage.tsx — new SignInAction component replacing the bare <Link>.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/pages/public/testDriveContent.ts — signedInNotice (tokenised {email}), signedInCta, signedOutBusy.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/pages/public/TestDrivePage.test.tsx — Map-backed localStorage shim + 4 regression tests.

## Validation results
- ✅ Test Command cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit — exit 0.
- ✅ Signed-in visitor sees a "sign out to use your test account" guard rather than silently entering their own account — test asserts the guard names the account AND that the bare Sign-in link is gone (that link is what caused the bug).
- ✅ Logged-out path unchanged — same <Link>, same href, same classes; test-covered.
- ✅ No security change — UX guard only; reuses the canonical authAPI.logout().
- ✅ No regression — frontend 1619 passed / 225 files; eslint 1 warning before AND after (pre-existing import/order, verified by linting main's own copy).

## Decisions made
- Reused authAPI.logout() rather than a local clearAuthItems(). api/client is already in this page's chain (api/testDrive imports it), so nothing new is pulled in, and logout does the full job: server logout + supabase sign-out + clear. A local-only clear would leave the server session alive.
- Hard navigation after sign-out. Contexts in the tree still hold the old session; the login page must mount clean. Mirrors AppShell's sign-out.
- Guarded the storage read — a real bug, not a test detail. This is a PUBLIC page and getAuthItem does a bare localStorage.getItem, which throws in some private-browsing modes. Unguarded it crashed the whole credentials block, taking the tester's logins with it, over an optional convenience. Fails closed to "logged out" — i.e. the old behaviour. Found because it did exactly that in jsdom.
- Shimmed localStorage in the test (this jsdom has none) beside the existing matchMedia shim — for staging a session, NOT to hide the real failure mode, which has its own test.
- Did not pre-fill the generated credentials. The task listed it as "ideally": it means passing a real password through a URL or storage on a public page, and the validation criteria don't ask for it. Flagged as a follow-up rather than smuggled in.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1512.
2. Post-deploy, while signed in as admin: open /test-drive, provision a run, and look at the credentials block — expect "You're already signed in as admin@relopass.com" + a sign-out button, NOT a bare "Sign in →".
3. Click it — expect to land on the login page fully signed out, able to use the generated HR login.
4. In a private window (logged out), confirm the block still shows the plain "Sign in →".

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- Credential pre-fill / deep-link not done. The task called it "ideally"; it would put a real password in a URL or storage on a public page. Worth its own task with a decision on the mechanism.
- The guard reads the session once at mount. If a tester signs in elsewhere in another tab while this page is open, the block won't update until reload — acceptable: this block only renders after provisioning, and a session change needs a navigation anyway.
- The /auth page itself is untouched — the guard is at the point of departure (/test-drive), which is where the tester actually is. If someone reaches /auth directly with a live session, the old behaviour stands.

Execution order: 1 → 2 → (3 ∥ 4) → 5. Each DB stage is its own reversible, out-of-band migration per CLAUDE.md discipline. The resolver bridge stays until the invariants are proven in prod.

rows.title: CONTRACT extraction agent (reuse the merged employment_contract prompts)
rows.notes:
## What was built
An EMPLOYMENT_CONTRACT extraction agent (FR CDI/CDD, DE Arbeitsvertrag, NO arbeidskontrakt), registered in EXTRACTION_AGENT_REGISTRY and reachable from the orchestrator. It masks PII before the LLM call, recovers employer registry IDs on-platform, and emits 11 fields with per-field confidence. PR #1754.

## Files changed
- CREATED: backend/relopass/agents/extraction/employment_contract.py — the agent: jurisdiction detection, mask_pii before the LLM, raw-text registry-ID recovery, high/medium/low→float confidence, variable-pay text cross-check.
- MODIFIED: backend/relopass/agents/extraction/__init__.py — registry entry + a design record for why this is ONE code, not three.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/document_type_vocabulary.py — EMPLOYMENT_CONTRACT graduates from CLASSIFIER_PENDING_RUNTIME to CLASSIFIER_TO_RUNTIME + RUNTIME_DOCUMENT_TYPES.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/rce_document_ingest.py — contract filename tokens, placed LAST so the broad "contract" token cannot shadow lohnsteuer/passport.
- CREATED: backend/tests/test_extraction_employment_contract.py — 46 tests.
- CREATED: supabase/migrations/20261020000000_rce_employment_contract_document_type.sql — seeds the code.

## Validation results
- ✅ Criterion 1 (5 fields + per-field confidence) — 46/46 tests pass. NOTE: emitted with the PROMPT's names, not the criterion's — see Decisions. Satisfied semantically.
- ✅ Criterion 2 (mask_pii before the LLM) — test captures the prompt sent to the stub completer and asserts it is masked. See the known gap below.
- ✅ Criterion 3 (reachable, not merely defined) — _agent_class("EMPLOYMENT_CONTRACT") returns the class. Guard proven, not assumed: unregistering it fails test_extraction_agent_wiring naming "EmploymentContractAgent (employment_contract.py)"; passes again when restored.
- ✅ Criterion 4 (reuses the merged prompts) — no new prompt authored; all three .txt load and are asserted.
- ✅ Criterion 5 (fail-soft) — unparseable salary, non-contract payload, and undetectable locale all return a result and never raise.
- ✅ No regressions — full backend suite run on this branch AND on clean origin/main with identical env: zero failures unique to this branch (baseline actually had 6 more). CI "Backend tests (deterministic P1 suite)" passes.
- ✅ Migration validated against real Postgres in a rolled-back transaction; prod row count verified still 0.

## Decisions made
- Emitted the prompt's field names, not the criterion's. contradiction.py's COHORT_1_FIELD_KEYS is keyed on employer_legal_name and gross_salary_annual (±5% salary compare). Emitting employer_name/salary_amount would have broken contradiction detection silently. The vault-side translation belongs to the prefill-sourcing task — that bridge does not exist in the repo today.
- ONE code for three locales, NOT the TAX_CERT split. AIQ-1774's lesson was "never require a signal nothing supplies"; here the signal is the document's own language, already in the text the agent reads. A split is also unmappable — the classifier emits one EMPLOYMENT_CONTRACT code and names the three as variants of it — and unlike tax certs, the three prompts share one output schema.
- Masked, then recovered registry IDs on-platform. Measured: mask_pii('SIREN 552 120 222') → 'SIREN [REDACTED_PHONE]' (same for NO organisasjonsnummer). Salaries, dates, job titles and company names all survive. Recovery reads raw text in-process, which never leaves the platform, so the NO data sheet's employer_org_number still fills.
- Did not port the orphaned agent wholesale. Branch feat/c1-05c-employment-contract-agent (no PR, 1705 commits stale) had a 461-line agent written against an OLDER prompt draft — it reads gross_salary/salary_period/currency, none of which the merged prompt emits, so salary would have been silently null. Harvested its useful parts; wrote the rest fresh.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1754 — focus on the three decisions above, especially the ONE-code choice, which deliberately departs from the AIQ-1774 precedent.
2. pytest backend/tests/test_extraction_employment_contract.py -v → expect 46 passed.
3. Apply the migration out-of-band to create the rce.document_types row; merging does NOT create it. Note 20261019000000 (tax-cert split) is also still unapplied.
4. Decide on the masker gap below — accept as-is, or file the NER follow-up.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- PII: bare un-cued names still reach the LLM. mask_pii's name detector is context-boosted — it fires on an honorific (Madame/Frau/herr) or a name cue (født), so "og Olav Hansen" survives. This is the shared masker's documented limitation (its docstring defers bare names to a presidio+spaCy pass) and affects EVERY LLM path, not just this agent, so it was not patched here. test_uncued_person_name_is_a_known_masker_gap pins it so it is visible in CI and fails loudly when the NER pass lands. Worth filing as its own task.
- This agent cannot run on real documents yet. rce.documents is empty in prod and the bridge no-ops because nothing has written an rce.cases row since 2026-06-30 (AIQ-1780). Out of scope per this task's own instruction.
- CI blocker, not mine: "Migration ledger drift check" fails on prod version 20260805214336 brain3c_supplier_qualification, which has no repo file — drift in the OPPOSITE direction from this PR. Its applied SQL is still recoverable from schema_migrations.statements (1 statement), so a prod-as-oracle reconciliation migration would clear it. "RLS coverage check" fails on exception_requests (also failed on PR #1749). Both pre-existing and shared across all migration PRs.
- Out of scope: the vault/prefill translation layer; per-field bboxes (prompt emits 0–1 normalised, ExtractedField validates 0–1000); expanding the C1-04a classifier prompt.

rows.title: Operate FR→NO fact pipeline: run extractor → pending → commit eval report
rows.notes:
OWNER DECISIONS, 2026-08-12 — recorded so they are not re-litigated:

1. THE APPROVED FACTS: ACCEPTED AS-IS. Owner accepts them on the evidence — official government sources, an evidence_quote on every row, and a discriminating rather than blanket review (303 high-confidence rows left pending while 12 medium ones were approved, and rows were rejected). None of them cover FR-DE or FR-NO, so nothing customer-facing depends on them today. Do NOT re-open this as a data-quality question; it was examined and accepted.

2. THE RUNNING INGEST: LEFT RUNNING. Rows continue to arrive for non-corridor destinations. Owner's call: pending facts are not user-visible, so a growing pile costs storage and review time and nothing else.

—— CORRECTION 2026-08-12, later the same day ——

An earlier version of this note said the approver of those facts was "not recorded and cannot be reconstructed" because the schema had nowhere to put it. That was wrong, and the truth is sharper.

public.requirement_reviews EXISTS and is designed for exactly this — fact_id, reviewer_user_id, action, notes, created_at — and backend/db/policies.py:1404 writes a row to it in the SAME TRANSACTION as the status change. So an approval made through the application is always attributable.

Measured in prod: 91 approved facts, 0 requirement_reviews rows, 0 requirement_facts audit_logs rows. The audit path was not missing. IT WAS BYPASSED — the approvals were applied by direct database writes outside the application.

What this does and does not change:
- The owner's decision to accept the facts STANDS. It rested on source quality and evidence quotes, and that evidence is unaffected.
- What the owner accepted was the FACTS, not a bypassed audit path. Those are separate, and the second was not put to them at the time because it had not yet been found.
- The approvals were still increasing during the run (86 → 91), so whatever is doing this is live.

See AIQ-1823 for the full disproof, and the separately filed uuid bug — requirement_reviews.reviewer_user_id is uuid NOT NULL while admin.py:495 passes a TEXT actor, so the proper approve path would 500 for most admins even if someone used it.

STILL OPEN, and why this ticket should not simply be closed: the FR-NO extraction run it actually asks for has not happened, and its acceptance criteria need rewriting against the real starting state — a table with 500+ rows in it, not an empty one — or the eval report will measure someone else's data.

rows.title: Roadmap paywall: payment_status backend fail-open — ent is None → roadmap_unlocked=true
rows.notes:
## What was built
The roadmap paywall now distinguishes "the entitlement store could not be consulted" from "the store answered and no case matches this id". The first still GRANTS access (deliberate, unchanged); the second now DENIES it. Both the enforcement gate and the status endpoint share one decision function, so they can no longer disagree about the same case.

PR: https://github.com/rlecomte1929/rolec/pull/1664 — branch fix/aiq-1699-payment-status-fail-closed, commit 08664d46.

## The ticket's premise was half right — scope changed accordingly (approved by Romain before implementing)

Confirmed: payment.py::payment_status did fail open on ent is None, exactly as described, and the paywall IS on in production (RELOPASS_ROADMAP_PAYWALL_ENABLED=true on srv-d7ku8agjs32c7386fm4g). So this was live, not theoretical.

Refuted — it was not "the last residual fail-open", and the proposed one-liner was unsafe:
1. payment_status is not the gate. It is what the UI reads. The enforcing path is assert_roadmap_access → is_roadmap_unlocked (backend/app/services/roadmap_entitlement.py:87-88), wired into the two roadmap content endpoints at backend/app/routers/cases_read.py:974 and :1039. It had the same ent is None fail-open. Fixing only payment_status would have hidden the button while GET /api/cases/{id}/roadmap kept serving the roadmap — and "hiding a button in React is not a paywall" is that module's own opening line.
2. resolve_entitlement returns None for three reasons, not one: blank id; a caught SQLAlchemyError (DB error / un-migrated column — a deliberate infrastructure fail-open, documented in the module docstring); and no matching row. The ticket's unlocked = (not roadmap_paywall_enabled()) or (ent is not None and tier in PAID_TIERS) collapses all three, so a transient pooler error would have paywalled a paying customer — the exact outcome the ticket's own Technical Constraints forbid.
3. The fail-open was pinned by a passing test (test_paywall_on_unresolved_fails_open), i.e. it was a design decision, not an oversight.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/roadmap_entitlement.py — new EntitlementLookup(row, available) NamedTuple and lookup_entitlement(); new unlocked_from_lookup() as the single access decision; is_roadmap_unlocked() now denies on a resolved-but-unknown case and still short-circuits before any DB lookup when the flag is off; resolve_entitlement() retained as a row-only wrapper for non-gating callers; module docstring rewritten to state the two-outcome policy.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/routers/payment.py — payment_status uses lookup_entitlement + unlocked_from_lookup; dropped the now-unused PAID_TIERS / roadmap_paywall_enabled imports.
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_roadmap_entitlement.py — test_paywall_on_unresolved_fails_open split into test_paywall_on_store_unreachable_fails_open (still grants) and test_paywall_on_unknown_case_fails_closed (now denies); same split for the status endpoint; added test_blank_case_id_is_resolved_not_an_outage and a back-compat test for resolve_entitlement.
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_payment_status_assignment_id_access.py — repointed the entitlement stub at lookup_entitlement.

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) Paywall ON + case with no entitlement row → roadmap_unlocked=false (was true) — test_status_flag_on_unknown_case_fails_closed, plus test_paywall_on_unknown_case_fails_closed proving the enforcement path now raises 402 too.
- ✅ 2) Paid case still → true — test_paywall_on_paid_tier_unlocks (roadmap + essentials) and test_status_flag_on_paid_reports_unlocked.
- ✅ 3) Free case WITH a row still → false — test_paywall_on_free_tier_locks, test_status_flag_on_free_reports_locked, and the AIQ-1687 assignment-id test unchanged in outcome.
- ✅ 4) No legitimately-entitled case newly paywalled. Checked against production: every case_assignments row created in the last 20 days resolves to a relocation_cases row (206 of 207 in the window; the one exception is from 2026-07-06), all 11 paid cases have rows, and 0 relocation_cases rows have a NULL access_tier (so the migration is applied and the un-migrated-column fail-open is not live). Staged test-drive provisioning always produces a resolvable row, so the ticket's QA guardrail holds. resolve_entitlement's None behaviour for a valid provisioned case: it does not return None — that is why failing closed is safe.
- ✅ 5) pytest -k payment green — 10 passed. Also -k "roadmap or entitlement or paywall or checkout" → 329 passed / 1 skipped, and the full backend suite → 5599 passed (the 14 failures are the documented pre-existing llm_client asyncio baseline, untouched).

## Decisions made
- EntitlementLookup NamedTuple over raising an exception. An exception would make the fail-open depend on every caller remembering a try/except; an uncaught one would 500 a revenue endpoint. With the tuple, the worst a careless caller does is read .row and get today's behaviour.
- Kept resolve_entitlement as a wrapper. Nothing else calls it today, but keeping the name means a future caller that only wants the row isn't forced through the gating API.
- Tests now set the real env var instead of stubbing roadmap_paywall_enabled on the router. Once the decision moved into the service module, those router-level patches stopped controlling anything — leaving them would have let the tests pass for the wrong reason.
- Preserved the flag-off short-circuit. My first draft moved the lookup above the flag check, which would have added a DB query per roadmap request while the paywall is off. Caught by the existing test_paywall_off_is_always_unlocked guard and fixed.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1664 (4 files, +137/−43). The behaviour change worth eyeballing is unlocked_from_lookup in roadmap_entitlement.py.
2. After merge + deploy, confirm a real paid case still unlocks (case with access_tier='roadmap') and that a garbage id now returns roadmap_unlocked=false from GET /api/payment/status/{id}.
3. Note that 24 legacy/demo assignments with a dangling canonical_case_id lose their free roadmap. All pre-launch fixtures — but if any is used in a QA runbook, it will now hit the paywall.

## Known gaps / follow-up

- payment_status still issues its own lookup rather than reusing the gate's, so a case is resolved twice across a page load (once for the status call, once when the roadmap is fetched). Negligible today; noting it rather than adding a cache.

rows.title: Recommendations: dedup registry-vs-static twins before the top_n cut (AIQ-1688 follow-up)
rows.notes:
## What was built
The recommendations engine no longer lets one supplier occupy two candidate slots. _load_dataset_with_registry now batch-resolves the registry candidates' masters via service_catalog_items.supplier_id (the link AIQ-1688 established) and drops any static-dataset item whose item_id is one of those masters' external_ids — before scoring and before the top_n cut. The registry representation is kept (richer data). The lookup is best-effort: if the catalog is unreachable the merge falls back to today's behaviour rather than blanking the category.

PR: https://github.com/rlecomte1929/rolec/pull/1661 — branch fix/aiq-1690-registry-static-twin-dedup, commit 7bc9451b.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/app/recommendations/engine.py — _load_dataset_with_registry skips static twins of registry candidates (also benefits recommend_debug, which shares the loader).
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/service_catalog.py — new external_ids_for_supplier_ids(category, supplier_ids), the batched form of find_master_by_supplier_or_external_id's supplier_id link; added the bindparam import for the expanding IN clause.
- CREATED: backend/tests/test_recommendations_registry_twin_dedup.py — 5 tests (twin dropped / non-twin still merged / no distinct supplier crowded out / lookup-failure fallback / registry-empty fallback).

## Validation results
- ✅ Criterion 1 — NL_SG returns up to top_n DISTINCT movers, none dropped because of a twin. Ran the shipped ranking + curation code against the real prod inputs (12 SG registry movers, their supplier_scoring_metadata, the 10 static m-* items, and company 12cc821f…'s 12 approved masters), stubbing only DB access. Before: 22 dataset rows / 12 distinct suppliers / 6 movers rendered. After: 12 rows / 12 distinct / 10 rendered (the full top_n), zero duplicate suppliers. The four movers previously crowded out by their own twins — Shalom Movers, Leo's Moving, Movers.sg, JK Movers — now render.
- ✅ Criterion 2 — unit test: registry item + static twin yields ONE candidate, registry preferred. test_static_twin_dropped_registry_representation_kept asserts [<supplier UUID>] and _source == 'supplier_registry'. Red before the fix (returned both rows), green after.
- ✅ Criterion 3 — regression: movers still render on NL_SG, hr_curation_status stays None; other corridors unaffected. The simulation above reports hr_curation_status = None in both the before and after runs. Non-twin static items still merge (test_static_item_without_registry_twin_still_merged), and the registry-empty static fallback is unchanged (test_registry_empty_uses_static_only).
- ✅ Criterion 4 — pytest -k "recommendation or movers or curation" green. 55 passed, 5676 deselected. Adjacent suites (-k "catalog or registry or supplier or engine"): 408 passed, 9 skipped. Full backend suite: 5586 passed / 14 failed — those 14 are the documented pre-existing test_llm_client* asyncio baseline plus test_policy_propagation and test_supabase_password_sync, all untouched by this change.
- ✅ Constraint — verify on real Postgres, not just SQLite. The new SQL was executed read-only against prod (nsvefcvpvwwwhuqyuqmp). service_catalog_items.supplier_id is character varying, so CAST(supplier_id AS TEXT) matches the existing find_master_by_supplier_or_external_id pattern; for the 12 SG movers supplier ids it returns exactly m-1…m-10 plus the two self-keyed masters (SIRVA, Delahaye), which were already deduped by item_id.

## Decisions made
- Kept the change category-agnostic. The dedup is driven purely by the supplier_id link, so any category with registry + static twins gets it; nothing special-cases movers.
- Wrapped the master lookup in try/except. The rest of _load_dataset_with_registry is already best-effort about DB access (the registry search itself swallows exceptions). A catalog outage must degrade to the old merge, never to an empty category — that failure mode is exactly the AIQ-1688 symptom.
- Left the "curate before top_n" refactor out, as the ticket scoped it. It changes every category's result size and deserves its own ticket.
- Did not add the twin ids to existing_ids. They are static ids being skipped, not candidates being admitted; conflating them would change nothing today but would be misleading.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1661 (3 files, +206/−2) and let CI run.
2. After merge + deploy, open the NL_SG (Amsterdam→Singapore) test case's Recommendations → Movers and confirm 10 distinct movers render (it was 6), with no repeated supplier name.
3. Spot-check one other corridor that mixes registry and static suppliers (e.g. an Oslo case, masters no-mv-1/no-mv-2) to confirm nothing regressed there.

rows.title: Redesign /hr/service-providers page UX for HR workflow
rows.notes:
# UX Redesign Spec — /hr/service-providers (AIQ-1602)

Deliverable = this spec (no production code, per the task). Grounded in a full repo recon 2026-07-18. The page today = HrServiceProvidersPage.tsx with 3 tabs (Dashboard / Vendor Management=HrVendorCuration.tsx / Vendor Performance). Hannah's 4-segment workflow maps onto existing machinery — two segments are UX-only, two have real backend gaps.

## Current state vs the 4 segments

Segment 1 — Filter & Discover — EXISTS (UX-only rework). Country/City/Category filters (HrVendorCuration.tsx:698-776); City is admin-allowlist-only (catalog_destination_allowlist), not free-text. Results = the admin master catalog service_catalog_items filtered by category (+city when geo-bound), de-duped by name (hr_catalog.py:162-186). This IS the ‘database of pre-selected providers’.

Segment 2 — Select & Validate — EXISTS (UX-only). Checkbox per master row → bulk ‘Save changes’ → POST /api/hr/catalog/curation/select → table company_vendor_selections (PER-COMPANY, not per-employee; keyed by company_id+category+master_item_id+destination_city). selected toggles employee visibility. HR can re-open and re-tick anytime. So ‘select, validate, add/remove later’ all already work.

Segment 3 — Gap Request — PARTIAL (real gap). ‘+ Request a new destination’ modal → populate-destination-with-ai → writes catalog_destination_requests (status pending) + an audit row. An admin queue EXISTS (GET/PATCH /api/admin/catalog/destination-requests; approve auto-adds to allowlist) and a pending_destination_requests badge count. BUT no active admin notification fires — no email, no in-app. The UI’s ‘We’ve notified our admin team’ copy is currently FALSE (admin only learns by polling the queue). Also today the request is per destination(+category); the redesign wants a request for a missing country/city/CATEGORY combo from an empty result set.

Segment 4 — Preferred Supplier Registration — WRONG TARGET (real gap + governance decision). Today ‘add custom vendor’ writes company_vendor_selections (HR/company-scoped; only name + notes collected). It does NOT reach the admin master (service_catalog_items) or the suppliers registry. Hannah explicitly wants it to ‘populate the main admin database’. The admin master supplier form already exists to mirror: AdminSupplierNew.tsx → POST /api/suppliers (require_admin) → suppliers table (+ supplier_capabilities, supplier_scoring). Fields: name, legal_name, status, description, website, contact_email, contact_phone, languages[], verified; per-capability service_category, coverage scope (global/country/city), country/city, tags[], min/max_budget, family_support, remote_support; scoring rating/review_count/SLA/preferred/premium. A bridge already exists: POST /api/admin/catalog/promote-hr-vendors.

Cross-cutting — /api/notifications is DEAD. Confirmed 500 in prod (notifications.user_id is uuid but legacy HR ids are text; 424 rows unreadable; documented in roadmap_review_notification.py). This page does NOT depend on it (it uses /api/hr/catalog/notification-counts + /employee-demand, which work). The ONLY working push channel today is Resend email (_resend_send).

## Proposed layout (4 visually + functionally distinct segments)
Replace the 3-tab shell’s Vendor Management with a single guided column:
1. Top: Filter bar (Country → City → Category, cascading; City limited to allowlist with an inline ‘request a new city’ affordance). Sticky.
2. Results area — the filtered master list, each row a select toggle + ‘Approve for employees’; a persistent ‘Approved (N)’ summary + one ‘Save selection’ action with a confirmation toast. Loading = skeleton rows; error = inline retry.
3. Empty-state Gap-Request banner — shown ONLY when the filter returns 0 results: ‘No approved providers for {category} in {city}. Request that admin source them.’ → submits a catalog_destination_requests row for (country, city, category) AND (NEW) fires an admin email via Resend. Copy must reflect reality (‘Sent to admin — you’ll see them here once added’).
4. ‘Register a preferred supplier’ drawer (separate, clearly labelled) — a fuller form mirroring the admin suppliers fields, writing to the admin registry (see open question A on governance).

## Backend: exists vs needs
- EXISTS: curation view/select (`/api/hr/catalog/), destination requests + admin queue, admin supplier create (POST /api/suppliers), promote-hr-vendors bridge, catalog badge endpoints.
- NEEDS: (Seg 3) an admin-notify on open_destination_request — wire Resend email (do NOT use the dead /api/notifications). (Seg 4) a decision + endpoint for HR→admin supplier registration (see A).

## Open product questions (must answer before implementation)
A. **Governance — Segment 4 target.** Hannah wants HR supplier registration to ‘populate the main admin database’. Writing directly to the shared cross-tenant suppliers registry from an HR role is a trust boundary (an HR user could inject vendors other companies see). Options: (i) HR submits to a **moderation queue** (status=draft) that admin approves into suppliers (safest — mirrors the destination-request pattern + the existing promote-hr-vendors bridge); (ii) HR writes directly with source=‘hr_manual’ + verified=false (fast, riskier); (iii) keep company-scoped custom vendors (rejects the ask). Recommend (i).
B. **Employee scoping.** Selection is per-COMPANY today (all the company’s employees see the same approved set), not per-employee. Hannah says ‘the ones my employee will see’ (singular). Confirm: keep per-company, or add per-employee scoping (a schema change)?
C. **Gap-request notification channel.** /api/notifications is dead. Confirm Resend email to admin is acceptable for gap requests (recommended), vs waiting on an in-app-notifications fix (separate, larger task).
D. **Required supplier fields for HR.** Which of the admin suppliers` fields are mandatory for an HR-submitted supplier (name + category + coverage + contact at minimum)?

## Validation criteria coverage
1. All 4 segments covered ✅ · 2. Per-segment affordance/action/response/empty+error states ✅ · 3. Endpoints exist-vs-new enumerated ✅ · 4. /api/notifications 500 flagged as the Seg-3 dependency risk (dead; use Resend) ✅ · 5. Open product questions enumerated (A-D) ✅ · 6. Layout makes the 4 segments distinct ✅.

## Recommendation
Close as Done (research/spec complete). Implementation should be split into follow-up tickets: Seg 3 admin-notify (small), Seg 4 HR→admin supplier moderation queue (medium, needs decision A), and a UX pass on Seg 1/2 layout. The AIQ-1579 proposal (earlier) overlaps and should be merged into this.

|---|---|---|

The pre-fix trigger_rules jsonb for all three templates was recorded verbatim before being overwritten. STILL BLOCKED, deliberately not smuggled in: the named-employer / outbound target-account list from Segment B downloads. That genuinely requires campaign data. It stays behind ADS-6 / ADS-1.

rows.title: Case-id guard scans 4 routers but 38 live functions match its criterion — widen _ROUTERS + correct the audit doc
rows.notes:
## Done — PR #1744 (branch fix/aiq-1775-widen-caseid-guard, commit 350e4371)

### Measurement reproduced independently
Ran the guard's OWN _CASE_SQL regex + _RESOLVERS + _resolves predicate over every router rather than trusting the ticket:
  total matches      60   (task claimed 60) ✅ exact
  live routers       40   (task claimed 38)
  cases.py unwired   20   (task claimed 22)
The live/unwired split drifted by 2 because main moved since the task's 82c03aaa snapshot — which is itself the point: the blind spot grew with every merge. Used my numbers, as the task instructed.

### Validation results (all 5 criteria)
1. PASS — all 40 live functions classified. 13 safe (with reasons), 29 known-unsafe (with refs). Zero unclassified.
2. PASS — the guard now scans every router, DERIVED not hardcoded. test_scope_is_derived_not_hardcoded fails if anyone reverts to a literal list.
3. PASS — CASE_ID_RESOLUTION_AUDIT.md no longer claims 'closed structurally'. It states actual coverage, the 13/29 split, the root cause, and that the class is NOT closed until the register empties.
4. PASS — cases.py excluded via a named _UNWIRED set citing backend/main.py:136, with a note to delete the exclusion if it is re-wired.
5. PASS — no behaviour change. Test + docs only.

### The design decision that matters: TWO registers, not one
_ALLOWLIST (13, safe) and _KNOWN_UNRESOLVED (29, unsafe) are separate dicts. Folding the 29 into the allowlist would have turned the guard green while implying they were reviewed and found safe — they were reviewed and found UNSAFE. The task explicitly warned against mass-allowlisting; this is how I avoided it without leaving the test red. Two tests enforce the discipline: the register can only shrink, and the two registers must be disjoint.

### Root cause (shared by 12 of the 29)
_assert_case_access(user, case_id) at case_service.py:147 accepts EITHER a public.cases UUID OR an assignment_id — its docstring says so — and returns None rather than the resolved id. Callers validate access for either form, then run WHERE case_id = :raw_value. Pass an assignment id: access passes, SQL matches nothing, silent-empty. require_case_access (auth_deps.py:245) has the same shape but DOES return the assignment row; its 5 callers could derive the canonical id and don't.

Already shipped, not hypothetical: employee_quotes.list_hr_quote_requests documents in its own docstring that it is keyed on the canonical case_id while the HR route param is an assignment id — 0 of 51 rows matched, and its only frontend caller showed an empty panel for every case and was removed.

### Red-first evidence
Had _KNOWN_UNRESOLVED been empty, widening the scope would have failed the guard with 29 offenders. That is the proof the widening found real, previously-invisible gaps rather than being a no-op.

### Tests
7 passed. The 3 failures in test_case_id_resolution_a2.py are IDENTICAL on pristine origin/main (missing fastapi in the local offline env) — verified in a clean worktree, unrelated to this change.

### FOLLOW-UP NEEDED (the actual debt)
Fixing the 29 is out of scope here per Validation Criterion 5 — 29 endpoints across 9 routers is too large a blast radius for one PR. Recommend a task per router-group, starting with the 12 _assert_case_access callers, since they share one root cause and could plausibly be fixed by making that helper return the resolved id instead of None.

rows.title: HR user cannot send new destination request to admin
rows.notes:
## Root cause CONFIRMED (verified against prod nsvefcvpvwwwhuqyuqmp)
NOT a CORS/auth/registration issue. POST /api/hr/catalog/populate-destination-with-ai → for a NEW (off-allowlist) destination it calls scrape_safety.open_destination_request, which INSERTs into public.catalog_destination_requests. That table's requested_by column is uuid NOT NULL, but the endpoint writes user['id'] (the app-level HR id), which is legacy TEXT for some accounts. Reproduced the exact failure on prod (rolled back):

> INSERT ... requested_by='seed-hr-testingapril' → ERROR: 22P02: invalid input syntax for type uuid

The origin 500 has its CORS headers stripped by Cloudflare → the browser reports a network-level status-0 / 'access to server' error — exactly the symptom. 2 of 1451 public.users rows have non-uuid ids, so it is reachable. (The status-0 on /api/hr/assignments in the buffer is a separate/earlier call — not this flow.)

## Fix (recommended) — 🔴 migration
Mirror the established repo pattern (notifications / hr_supplier_submissions migrated user-id cols uuid→text):
sql
ALTER TABLE public.catalog_destination_requests
  ALTER COLUMN requested_by TYPE text USING requested_by::text,
  ALTER COLUMN resolved_by  TYPE text USING resolved_by::text;

- company_id stays uuid (companies.id is uuid; the cdr_update_hr_or_admin RLS policy uses company_id — unchanged).
- No FK constraints on the table; RLS policies do NOT reference requested_by — the change is safe and the cast is lossless.
- No code change strictly required (the app already passes the text id); optionally add an is-uuid note, but the column type is the real fix.

## Why no code-only stopgap
requested_by is uuid NOT NULL — can't insert NULL for a legacy id, and can't fabricate a uuid. The column type must change.

## Gate
🔴 Database Migration — needs human go, and per migration discipline it is applied out-of-band by the operator (NOT via MCP apply_migration). Deliverable = the migration file + PR; prod is fixed when the operator applies it + reconciles the ledger.

rows.title: The id-resolution guard is blind to the CAST(case_id AS TEXT) form — two unresolved handlers pass it today
rows.notes:
## What was built
The AIQ-1704 guard can now see the CAST(case_id AS TEXT) = :cid predicate style, and the two handlers that were hiding behind that blind spot — get_case_rfqs and dispatch_case_rfq — now resolve any of the three id forms before their tenant gate.

PR #1688, branch fix/aiq-1735-guard-cast-form, commit c3fd38aa.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_case_id_resolution_guard.py — widened _CASE_SQL to the three predicate styles (case_id = :, CAST(case_id AS TEXT) = :, case_id::text = :), anchored on \b so canonical_case_id is not a false positive; added CaseSqlPatternTests pinning all three styles plus two lookalikes that must NOT flag.
- MODIFIED: backend/app/routers/hr_coordination.py — get_case_rfqs and dispatch_case_rfq resolve via db.resolve_case_ids before the UNION tenant gate.
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_hr_case_rfqs.py — harness models the new call; 2 new tests (assignment id resolves and returns the RFQ; unresolvable id still 404s).
- MODIFIED: backend/tests/test_hr_rfq_dispatch.py — harness models the new call.

## Validation results
- ✅ 1) The regex flags all three styles. CaseSqlPatternTests::test_matches_every_predicate_style_the_codebase_writes asserts the pattern directly, plus test_does_not_flag_lookalikes for canonical_case_id, CAST(id AS TEXT) and a bare SELECT.
- ✅ 2) Blind spot reproduced before any fix. Guard GREEN on main (2 passed) while an AST walk showed get_case_rfqs / dispatch_case_rfq unresolved and unflagged. With the widened regex and no handler change, the guard FAILED with exactly ['dispatch_case_rfq', 'get_case_rfqs'] — and nothing else across all four scanned routers, so the blind spot was precisely characterised rather than guessed.
- ✅ 3) Green after the fix — guard 4 passed.
- ✅ 4) TEETH in the previously-invisible style. A synthetic WHERE CAST(case_id AS TEXT) = :cid handler fails the widened guard; I separately confirmed the OLD regex returns False on that exact string. Removed → green.
- ✅ 5) No false positives — full guard run green across every scanned router; the lookalike test guards the canonical_case_id case explicitly.
- ✅ 6) Test Command — guard 4 passed; -k 'case_id or rfq or coordination' → 111 passed. Full backend suite → 5665 passed (14 failures = documented pre-existing llm_client asyncio baseline).
- ✅ Real-world proof (production, read-only) on the RUN 004-V fixture from docs/claude-code-hr-rfq-dispatch-id-fix.md: assignment f515f4ec-37e8-4919-be2b-f59e1631bf6b → 0 rfqs; its canonical case 46e15d6c-880a-4e0a-97bf-6da001375f1d → 1. Exactly the ids the brief names.
- ✅ CI on #1688: Backend tests, Route-auth audit, Deliverable integrity, Secret scan, Compliance guard, Queue hygiene all green.

## Decisions made
- Resolve BEFORE the tenant gate, not instead of it. The UNION over relocation_cases/cases remains the authorization check, so resolution widened while authorization did not — an unresolvable id still falls through and 404s, and a case with no case_assignments row (the HR-wizard shape) is untouched. A new test pins the 404.
- Fixed rather than allowlisted. The task allowed either; allowlisting the two handlers would have left the actual 404 in place while making the guard look clean, which is the exact pathology this ticket exists to remove.
- Anchored the regex on \b. Without it, canonical_case_id = :cid would flag — a false positive on already-correct code. A guard that cries wolf gets deleted, so the lookalike test is as load-bearing as the positive one.
- Patched the two test harnesses rather than making the handler Mock-defensive. conftest makes db a MagicMock; letting a test artefact shape production code would be the wrong trade.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1688 (4 files, +128/−1).
2. Merge PR #1670 too — it is the client half of the same 404 and is not superseded by this. This makes the id correct at the source; #1670 adds the fail-closed rendering.
3. To re-prove the teeth: append a function to hr_coordination.py containing WHERE CAST(case_id AS TEXT) = :cid with no resolver, run the guard — it must fail — then remove it.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- The guard is still a source-level check: it proves a resolver is called, not that the resolved id is the one actually bound in every query in that function. A handler could resolve and then bind the raw id anyway. Tightening that needs dataflow analysis, which is a different (and much larger) tool.
- _ROUTERS remains a hand-maintained list of four files. A case-scoped endpoint in an unlisted router is still invisible. Widening it to all of backend/app/routers/ would be the next increment, and would likely surface a batch of true positives worth their own ticket.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.title: BUG: exception inbox can show one benefit twice in mismatched currencies (NOK vs USD) across surfaces
rows.notes:
CORE PREMISE FALSE — no code change made (currency-normalization would be wrong; see below).

Verified: the 'HR inbox shows one benefit twice in mismatched currencies' scenario is already PREVENTED. Both surfaces (BenefitComparisonDashboard + PackageSummary) (a) load ALL of the case's exception-requests via listExceptionRequestsForCase, (b) gate the 'Request exception' CTA on an existing request for that key ('An existing request pre-empts the CTA' — BCD:257, PackageSummary:603), and (c) operate in the SAME canonical vocabulary: backend service_key IS canonical (service_comparison_engine.py:19,128), and PackageSummary explicitly canonicalizes its backendKey ('living_areas'->'housing') to match. So filing from either surface makes the OTHER show a pending badge, not a second CTA — the same benefit can't produce two requests. My original QA finding overstated it (noted canonical dedupe-on-write but missed the CTA gating + shared vocabulary).

The estimate page's currency='USD' (PackageSummary:672) is GENUINELY correct — its caps are convertToUsd-normalised; forcing native currency there would break its math.

TWO OPTIONAL minor residuals (NOT the filed bug — close or pursue?):
1. BCD keys its existing-requests map by RAW row.category (BCD:110) not canonicalServiceKey(row.category). Harmless today (all filings are canonical); a 1-line hardening would defend against any future non-canonical category. 
2. HR sees USD amounts for exceptions filed from the estimate page vs native from /employee/benefits. Minor display-consistency preference; making it always-native needs the estimate page's pre-USD amounts (larger change).

Recommend: close as not-a-bug, or greenlight the 1-line BCD:110 hardening if you want belt-and-suspenders.

rows.title: Intent-based onboarding router (replace generic dashboard)
rows.notes:
## Outcome: already shipped — duplicate of AIQ-829 (PR #592) + PR #1507. No code written.

The task's premise is that ReloPass lands every user on a generic dashboard and needs a routing question added. That is not the current state. Both halves — the routing question and the role-specific landing views — shipped months ago, and all three Validation Criteria are already satisfied on origin/main.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main, not from the commit messages)

1. The routing question exists. frontend/src/pages/Auth.tsx:574-596 renders exactly the question this task describes — label "I am…" with two options: 🏢 "An HR or mobility manager" ("Set up policies and manage relocations") and ✈️ "An employee being relocated" ("Track your move and tasks"). Shipped by AIQ-829 / PR #592. Choosing HR additionally reveals Company + company-size band.

2. Post-login routing already branches per role — there is no generic dashboard. frontend/src/navigation/routes.ts:247-254 homeRouteKeyForRole() maps EMPLOYEE→employeeDashboard, HR→hrDashboard, ADMIN→adminConsole; frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:45-49 calls it as redirectByRole() on every login. A legacy /dashboard route exists but no auth path ever navigates to it.

3. Role-specific first-login views exist. frontend/src/pages/hr/HrWelcomePage.tsx ("Set up your company workspace") and frontend/src/pages/employee/EmployeeWelcomePage.tsx ("Your relocation starts here"), routed at /hr/welcome and /employee/welcome, triggered by frontend/src/hooks/useWelcomeRedirect.ts on first login only. Shipped by PR #1507. Tests already exist (frontend/src/utils/welcomeSeen.test.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useWelcomeRedirect.test.tsx, frontend/src/pages/hr/HrWelcomePage.test.tsx).

## Validation results
- ✅ "First-time user sees the routing question" — satisfied at signup (Auth.tsx:574).
- ✅ "Selecting a role renders the matching role-specific view" — satisfied (homeRouteKeyForRole + the two welcome pages).
- ✅ "Choice persists across sessions; returning users skip straight to their role view" — satisfied. Role persists server-side in users.role / profiles.role / public.user_roles; the welcome page is shown once.

## Decisions made
- Did not move the question to post-login. The task's wording says "post-login flow replaced with a routing question", and the only literal gap is that placement. Implementing it would be wrong: a user's role is server-assigned (backend/app/routers/auth.py:238-249 — set at register from the invite, with ADMIN forced back to EMPLOYEE unless @relopass.com + allowlisted) and enforced by route guards. A post-login "are you HR or an employee?" prompt could not actually change anyone's role — it would either be cosmetic or, if it did write the role, become a privilege-escalation path. HR-invited employees deliberately never see the question; their role comes from the invitation (AIQ-829's stated design).
- Recorded the source-of-idea risk. This task came from the Friday Digest (a generic SaaS-onboarding blog post, "+47% activation"). The pattern it prescribes assumes a self-serve product where the user picks their own role. ReloPass is B2B invite-based — the role arrives with the invitation. Worth weighting digest-sourced tasks against product reality before queueing them.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- One real defect found while verifying (filed separately as AIQ-1701): the first-login welcome dismissal is persisted in localStorage['relopass_welcome_seen_<userId>'] only (frontend/src/utils/welcomeSeen.ts:13-28) — there is no profiles.onboarding_completed column anywhere in the repo. A returning user on a new browser, a new device, or in incognito sees the welcome page again. Small, real, and genuinely in the spirit of this task's third criterion.

Read the Expected Output mismatch first. This task asked for "a selector that routes a TAX_CERT document to the correct country agent". No selector was built. That is the approved decision, not a shortcut — but it is a Red-tier task, so the Done call is yours.

## Why no selector
AIQ-1745 already proved (Phase 2.5) that no country signal reaches the selection point: no country column on rce.documents; language is dead schema (never written); 0 rows to content-detect from; and the case corridor is genuinely ambiguous — an FR→NO case legitimately receives BOTH an FR and an NO certificate. That last point is fatal to any per-case selector, which is what made splitting the code the right answer rather than a workaround.

A German Lohnsteuerbescheinigung, a French avis d'imposition and a Norwegian skattemelding are genuinely different documents. Different codes, flat registry, no selector, no new signal to thread anywhere.

## Validation results
- PASS (1) Per-country routing asserted individually — _agent_class("TAX_CERT_DE") is TaxCertDeAgent, and FR/NO likewise. Routed by code rather than by a country argument; the asserted outcome is exactly what the criterion demanded.
- PASS (2) No silent default. test_bare_tax_cert_still_refuses_to_guess holds the retired code unrouted, and an ambiguous "tax" filename now returns None rather than guessing a locale → skipped_no_agent, as before.
- PARTIAL (3) All three ARE reachable and the equivalent guard is green — but the named artifacts UNREACHABLE_AGENTS / test_unreachable_list_stays_honest do not exist on main. They were from an unmerged variant. The merged guard is test_every_agent_class_has_a_route, which discovers agent classes by walking modules and fails if any lacks a route.
- PASS (4) Other 6 agents unaffected — test_existing_registrations_unchanged green.
- PASS (5) No new input needed; the design removes the requirement rather than defaulting it.

Guard proven, not assumed: unregistering TaxCertFrAgent fails three independent tests naming the agent; restored → green. Full sweep 116 passed, 9 xfailed.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: backend/relopass/agents/extraction/__init__.py — three registry entries; TAX_CERT_AGENTS_BY_ISSUING_COUNTRY + TAX_CERT_DOCUMENT_TYPE deleted (verified nothing else used them)
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/rce_extraction_orchestrator.py — TAX_CERT special case and the issuing_country param removed from _agent_class / dispatch_and_run / run_extraction_for_document
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/rce_document_ingest.py — filename heuristic split by locale
- MODIFIED: backend/app/services/document_type_vocabulary.py, backend/tests/test_extraction_agent_wiring.py, backend/tests/test_rce_document_ingest.py, the three backend/relopass/agents/extraction/tax_cert_{de,fr,no}.py, apps/hr-dashboard/src/features/resolution/CandidateCard.tsx
- CREATED: supabase/migrations/20261019000000_rce_tax_cert_split_by_locale.sql

## Decisions made
- The codes are producible today. rce_document_ingest's filename heuristic already carried locale tokens; now split (lohnsteuer→DE, avis→FR, skatte→NO). A bare "tax" returns None rather than guessing — not a regression, since it previously produced a code that routed to no agent.
- The classifier prompt was deliberately NOT expanded. prompts/docs/classifier/v1.txt declares itself the Cohort-1 subset and puts tax certificates out of scope; its eval fixture F10 asserts a DE Lohnsteuerbescheinigung MUST return UNKNOWN. Adding three codes would take it 10→13 classes, invert a gold fixture and invalidate the ≥9/10 + F10=UNKNOWN gate. That is a Cohort-2 scope change with its own eval.
- The bare TAX_CERT delete is guarded, not unconditional — if any document references it at apply time the row is kept and a NOTICE is raised.

## What the reviewer should do

2. Apply the migration to prod — merging does not create the rows. Until then the three agents remain unreachable in production.

rows.title: Decide the single owner of document extraction (immigration_documents-OCR vs rce)
rows.notes:
## RULED 2026-08-04 by Romain — recommendation ACCEPTED

Decision: rce owns document extraction. document_extraction_queue is NARROWED, not deleted.

The analysis (docs/architecture/EXTRACTION_PIPELINE_OWNER.md, merged 4b47bb45) showed the parent's "two rival pipelines, pick one" framing did not match the code: one router fires both, and the rce path imports its classifier FROM the path the parent proposed deleting (rce_ocr_parser.py:184). Deleting it would have removed a function rce itself calls.

### What the ruling authorises, in order
1. Move classify_document to a neutral module — the concrete first step, and the reason "narrow" beats "delete". Must happen BEFORE AIQ-1768 so the real classifier is written once, in its final home rather than in a module being wound down.
2. AIQ-1766 / AIQ-1767 / AIQ-1768 → unblocked, targeting rce.
3. document_extraction_queue keeps OCR ingest only.

### How the empty-table evidence was weighted (recorded so it can be revisited)
rce.documents has 0 rows, which reads as an argument to deprecate rce. Weighted the other way: the trigger at immigration_documents.py:122 needs a bridge that has never opened, so emptiness reflects an unfired feature flag rather than a failed design. rce is the path with the agent registry, structured persistence, entity resolution and contradiction detection; the MVP path classifies by filename keyword and its own docstring calls itself a placeholder.

### Separate product question, deliberately NOT decided here
Whether to open the rce bridge for real uploads. Until it opens, the CONTRACT and PAYSLIP agents that AIQ-1766/1767 will build do not run on real documents. Worth deciding before investing heavily in them — flagged at ruling time, not discovered later.

### Related finding that landed alongside
Executing AIQ-1774 surfaced that the classifier and runtime vocabularies shared exactly ONE code (PASSPORT_TD3). Fixed in PR #1745 (bef3022c) — document_type_vocabulary.py is now the mapping AIQ-1768 must target. Without it, the classifier swap would have produced codes no agent could act on.

PREMISE: Refuted (the "two rival pipelines" framing)   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: docs

Fixed the --api-only gate in relopass_api_runner.js. main() gated ALL 14 non-auth suites behind if (!apiOnly) (line 868), so the flag documented at line 8 as 'skip scenario flows, API checks only' actually ran auth only — ~6 of 44 rows, while looking clean. Moved the gate boundary so the 12 API suites always run and only the 3 scenario suites (suitePersonaFlows, suiteT13AdminOnboarding, suiteT14FullStack) are skipped under --api-only.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: /Users/romainlecomte/.claude/skills/relopass-e2e-test/scripts/relopass_api_runner.js — main(), the gate boundary only. The if (!apiOnly) block now wraps just the 3 scenario suites. No suite body touched; call order unchanged.

NOTE: this is the E2E SKILL script, NOT the rolec repo — there is NO git commit/PR/GitHub diff. Deliverable = updated local script + a green run.

## The trap that was avoided
suiteT13AdminOnboarding (line 701) and suiteT14FullStack (line 764) each self-gate on targetScenarios.includes(...). Under --scenario ZZZ they no-op — which is why that workaround looked clean. But --api-only leaves targetScenarios at its ALL_SCENARIOS default (lines 78/87), so it INCLUDES 'T13'/'T14'. A naive 'move the closing brace to the end' fix would have STARTED running both heavy scenario suites under the flag meant to skip them. They were explicitly placed inside the new gate. Verified by M2 (zero scenario rows under --api-only).

## Validation results
- ✅ M5 node --check — PASS.
- ✅ M1 (intent: all 12 API suites run under --api-only) — PROVEN. Every API suite emitted rows: Auth 6, Cases 5, HR 3, Employee 1, Resources 2, Reliability 1, WizardPersistence 7, CORS 6, RateLimiting 1, XSS 1, Perf 6, RLSIsolation 1 = 40 rows. Before the fix --api-only emitted ~6 auth rows only.
- ⚠️ M1 (exact 44-row parity) — NOT confirmable live; see rate-limit finding below. Diffed the after-fix --api-only run against the clean 44-row baseline (results/test_results_2026-07-16T07-40.json): missing exactly RLS1, RLS2, RLS3, RLS4 and ZERO extra rows. That gap is fully explained — RLS0's HR2 registration 429'd, and suiteRLSIsolation early-returns at line 409 without its token, which by code inspection is the only thing gating RLS1-4. Not attributable to this change.
- ✅ M2 (zero scenario rows under --api-only) — PASS. 0 rows matching /FLOW$|^T13|^T14_/ or category 'Scenario'. This is the trap check.
- ✅ M3 (WZ4 present) — PASS. WZ4 status=PASS, actual=400. AIQ-1554's Test Command (--api-only # then check the WZ4 row) is now genuinely able to validate AIQ-1554, as-is, with no edit — as predicted.
- ✅ M4 (non-apiOnly path intact) — PASS. --scenario T13 still emits T13_B9=PASS, T13_B2_API=PASS, T13_B1_FRESH=SKIP, T13_FLOW=PASS.
- ➖ M6 (--api-only faster) — mechanism holds (persona flows skipped; --api-only ran in 44s) but NOT independently measured against a timed full run. Not claimed as verified.

## ⚠️ Discovered during validation — the runner can only run cleanly ONCE PER HOUR
The backend caps registration at @limiter.limit("5/hour;20/day") (rolec: backend/app/routers/auth.py:183). Each runner invocation registers 3 accounts (HR via AT2, employee via AT3, HR2 via RLS0). So the 2nd run in any rolling hour exceeds the cap and starts 429ing. Observed today, exactly consistent:
  - 07:40 run (registrations 1-3): clean, 44 rows, 41 PASS / 0 FAIL.
  - 07:51 run (4,5 ok; 6th 429): 40 rows — RLS0 SKIP, RLS1-4 lost.
  - 07:52 run (7,8,9 all 429): 28 rows — AT2/AT3 FAIL, cascading SKIPs across suiteHR/Wizard/XSS.
This makes back-to-back comparison runs impossible against prod and produces alarming-looking FAILs that are pure rate-limit artifacts — the same false-signal family as AIQ-1554 and this task. Worth its own ticket (e.g. reuse accounts across runs, or gate re-registration).

## What the reviewer should do
1. There is NO GitHub PR — the change is local to relopass_api_runner.js.
2. Wait for a clean register bucket (~1h after the last run), then node relopass_api_runner.js --api-only — expect 44 rows including WZ2-WZ5, CORS, RL1, SEC1, PERF1-6, RLS0-4, and zero T13_/T14_/_FLOW rows.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- The 5/hour register cap vs 3-registrations-per-run collision above (highest value follow-up).
- --scenario has the SAME doc/behaviour mismatch as the bug just fixed: line 6 documents --scenario T1 as 'single persona flow only', but it runs all API suites PLUS T1. Left alone deliberately — fixing it would break the --scenario ZZZ workaround and is a separate call.
- bugMap || short-circuit (lines ~903/906): B5: CT3 || RLS1 — a truthy 'WARN'/'SKIP' string short-circuits before the RLS fallback, so B5/B8 report CT3/HP2's non-PASS even when RLS1/RLS3 passed. Only undefined triggers the intended fallback. Real bug, out of scope here.

rows.title: HR can't see/relay the supplier magic link — it surfaces only in the employee inbox thread
rows.notes:
## What was built
HR now sees and can copy each supplier's magic link immediately after dispatching, on the Provider Coordination panel. PR #1698, branch feat/aiq1743-hr-supplier-link, commit 4ecbb726. Frontend-only — no backend change, no new endpoint, no re-mint.

## Premise CONFIRMED, but the prescribed approach was wrong (Phase 2.5)

The bug is real. On the ticket's own example (RFQ-20260727-29700a5f, case c7f5f1e4), live prod shows the RFQ has ONE vendor_quote conversation with 12 messages, all from a single sender — the employee (emp-r4w1b-23aa@probe.test). No HR sender, no HR participant. get_case_rfqs returns only supplier_id / supplier_name / status / last_activity_at per recipient. HR was genuinely blind.

Two corrections that made the fix much smaller than "Medium" implied:

1. "Read the existing token/link data (rfq_recipients)" is not possible. That table persists only sha256(token) — "The raw token is never stored" (20260921000000_supplier_magic_link.sql). The link cannot be read back, and re-minting issues a different JWT that invalidates the already-delivered link and rewinds funnel state (status='sent', new expires_at). That path was a dead end and would have been destructive.
2. The link was already on the wire to HR. dispatch_supplier_links appends "link": link to every result and dispatch_case_rfq returns results verbatim. The TS type DispatchRfqTargetResult simply omitted the field — HR's own client received every magic link on every dispatch and discarded it.

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/api/hrCoordination.ts — declare link?: string | null on DispatchRfqTargetResult, documented as a bearer credential that must never be persisted client-side.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/components/ProviderCoordinationPanel.tsx — new DispatchedSupplierLinks block; both dispatch handlers now keep res.results. Clipboard pattern reused from CaseEssentialsCard.tsx:33-43.
- CREATED: frontend/src/components/__tests__/ProviderCoordinationPanel.supplierLinks.test.tsx — 5 tests.

## Validation results
- ✅ HR can see and copy each supplier's magic link from an HR surface — copy buttons render per recipient after dispatch; test asserts the exact link string reaches the clipboard.
- ✅ Test Command cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build → No errors found / built in 4.01s.
- ✅ Red-before-green — discarding res.results again fails 3 of the 5 tests.
- ✅ No email egress / no new dispatch path — zero backend change; send_email untouched and still defaults false.
- ✅ No cross-tenant exposure — links come only from the response to HR's own dispatch_case_rfq call, which is already require_admin_or_hr + org-gated (404 on another company's case).
- ✅ Regression sweep src/components src/api + HrCommandCenterCaseDetail.rfqRead → 258 passed, 0 failed.
- ⚠️ Employee-inbox surfacing still works — unchanged by construction (no backend touched), but not re-exercised end-to-end here.

## Decisions made
- Session-scoped links, stated in the UI. The raw token is never persisted server-side, so it is not persisted client-side either. The panel says plainly that links vanish on reload, that re-dispatching issues fresh links and invalidates these, and that anyone holding a link can submit that supplier's quote.
- Rendered as its own block, NOT a copy cell on each recipient row. Dispatch results key on recipient_id; rfq.recipients rows key on supplier_id. The only shared field is the display name — joining on it would show supplier A's bearer token on supplier B's row when two share a name. A wrong credential on the wrong supplier is not cosmetic, so nothing is joined. A dedicated test pins this.
- The email path surfaces links too: when a send is skipped (unverified address, no RESEND key) the copyable link is the only way HR can still reach that supplier.
- Rejected: re-mint on demand — it would kill the link already delivered to the supplier and rewind their funnel state.

## Security assessment (recorded deliberately)
The token grants exactly two capabilities, scoped to one (rfq, recipient) pair: read that brief, and submit one quote (409 afterwards, enforced in require_supplier_link). No case/employee PII, no cross-RFQ replay. Surfacing it gives HR no capability they lacked — it was already in the response they trigger, and supplier_link_dispatch already comments that the link is "Returned so a human can review it, or open it themselves."

Pre-existing gap worth naming: HR can both submit supplier quotes (via any link) and approve the winning quote (PATCH /api/rfqs/{id}/quotes/{qid}/accept is HR-only). That segregation-of-duties weakness is not created by this change, but it is now easier to exercise. See follow-ups.

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1698 (3 files, frontend only).
2. On an HR case detail with an employee-submitted RFQ, click Dispatch to suppliers → a "Supplier links from this dispatch" block appears listing each supplier with a Copy link button.
3. Paste a copied link in a private window → it should open the supplier quote page for that supplier only.
4. Reload the case page → the links block is gone (expected: not stored).
5. Confirm the wording on credential-sharing is acceptable for HR-facing copy.

## Known gaps / follow-up tasks
- Links are session-only. If HR reloads before copying, they must dispatch again — which invalidates the links already delivered to suppliers. A durable surface would need a new endpoint reading the raw token back out of quote_messages.body (its only durable home); that is a materially larger security surface and was deliberately not built. Worth its own ticket if HR hits this in practice.
- Segregation of duties (above) — pre-existing; candidate for its own ticket.
- Re-dispatch mislabels a replied supplier. Re-minting sets status='sent' without clearing quote_submitted_at, so a supplier who already quoted shows as 'sent' while still being blocked (409) from quoting again. Pre-existing, untouched here.

PREMISE: Confirmed   DUPLICATE: no   OUTCOME: code

rows.title: Admin still sees analytics/privacy consent band — fix useIsAdmin() role resolution
rows.notes:
## What was built
Fixed the real reason an admin still saw the analytics/privacy consent band after AIQ-1660: ConsentBanner renders once at the app root and never remounts, while useIsAdmin() memoized the role read at first mount — so an admin who logged in during the same page load kept the stale pre-login value. Shipped in PR #1638 (branch fix/aiq1678-useisadmin-consent-band, commit 5eca6238).

## Files changed
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/features/admin/useIsAdmin.ts — read relopass_role FRESH each render (dropped the useMemo(..., [])), matching how AppShell reads it.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/components/ConsentBanner.tsx — subscribe to useLocation() so the root-mounted banner re-renders on the post-login navigation and re-applies the admin-hide.
- MODIFIED: frontend/src/components/__tests__/ConsentBanner.test.tsx — added a regression test (banner stays mounted, role set after mount, navigation must hide it).

## Validation results
- ✅ Root cause identified in code (Lead 2 — memo staleness at app-root mount). Leads 1 (email-allowlisted admin) and 3 (normalization mismatch) DISPROVEN: login writes normalizeStoredRole(user.role), the hook uppercases identically; and the admin resolved as admin for RequireAdminRoute (same hook), so it wasn't an allowlist gap.
- ✅ Admin session no longer renders the band; HR/Employee unchanged — npx vitest run ConsentBanner.test.tsx → 7 passed (incl. existing admin-hidden + HR-shows).
- ✅ No server-side authz change; useIsAdmin stays a cosmetic SEC-FE-4 hint.
- ✅ npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build clean.
- ✅ Regression test PROVEN: reverting only the two source files (keeping the new test) makes it FAIL (band stays); with the fix it passes.

## Decisions made
- Fixed the hook to read fresh (not memoized) rather than adding a role-change event bus — minimal, matches existing readers, and covers all consumers.
- Used useLocation() in ConsentBanner as the re-render trigger because login always navigates (redirectByRole); this avoids a new auth mechanism or data fetch (per the task constraints).

## What the reviewer should do
1. Review PR #1638: https://github.com/rlecomte1929/rolec/pull/1638
2. Optional manual check: in one page load, load the app signed-out (band visible for a fresh visitor), log in as admin, land on /admin — the band should now be absent.

## Known gaps / follow-up
- The original report (BUG-260722-D74A) may ALSO have been a stale cached bundle (filed shortly after the AIQ-1660 deploy). This fix addresses the genuine same-page-load-login defect regardless; if an admin still sees it after this ships + a hard refresh, capture their relopass_role value for a narrower look.
- Multi-role note: useIsAdmin gates on the ACTIVE role (relopass_role). An admin currently acting AS hr/employee (active role switched) will correctly see the band — that's expected, not a bug.
