rows.title: S2 · Derive required_lead_time_days() + feasibility verdict from the corridor step graph
rows.notes:
## Done — PR #1711 (branch feat/aiq-1748-corridor-feasibility, commit b1dafd8f)

⚠️ STACKED on PR #1710 (AIQ-1747). Base is feat/aiq-1747-arrival-anchor, NOT main. Merge #1710 first. Known trap: squash-merging a stacked PR's base auto-closes the child — retarget #1711 to main BEFORE merging #1710, or re-open it after.

### What was built
backend/relopass/corridors/feasibility.py — pure module (no DB, no clock, no app/ import):
- required_lead_time_days(steps): longest path from any root to the arrival_anchor. Reuses scheduler.schedule_steps rather than writing a second graph walk, so it inherits that function's cycle detection.
- assess_feasibility(steps, target_start_date, today) -> FeasibilityAssessment(verdict, required_days, available_days, derivation) with verdict in critical|tight|ok.

### Validation results (all 4 criteria PASS)
1. PASS — required_lead_time_days for ES_IE/CSEP_2026 == 104.
2. PASS — ES_IE at 90 days out -> critical; at 200 -> ok. Boundary also covered: 103 -> critical, 104 -> tight (exactly meeting the requirement is not 'not enough').
3. PASS — FR_NO and ES_NL (and all 6 other free-movement corridors) return ok at horizons 0, 7, 30, 90, 200. Asserted for all 8, not just the two named.
4. PASS — explicit tests assert the module source contains no 'backend.app' import and no date.today()/datetime.now(); today is always injected.

Suite: test_corridor_feasibility.py 15 passed. Full corridor + SLA suite 125 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failures.

### Design decisions worth reviewing
- MIN_MATERIAL_LEAD_DAYS (7): a corridor with under a week of pre-arrival steps is not lead-time constrained and always returns ok. Needed because free movement measures 1 day, and without this a same-day start would warn. Free movement is 0-1 and permit corridors 104-158, so this sits in an enormous gap — a noise guard, not a tuned parameter.
- TIGHT_BUFFER_DAYS (14): mirrors the existing scheduler.AMBER_THRESHOLD_DAYS, which plays the same role for per-step deadlines.
- Unassessable corridor (no anchor / no target date) returns None, NOT ok. An absent opinion must never render as reassurance.
- Verdict vocabulary kept distinct from scheduler's per-step flags (green/amber/red_late) because this is one verdict about the whole case, not a step classification.
- Not exported from corridors/init.py — follows the scheduler precedent (corridor_persistence imports schedule_steps directly from .scheduler).

### Tests load real YAMLs, not fixtures
Deliberate: the point of deriving from the step graph is that it tracks corridor content, so a duration edit must BREAK the test rather than let it drift. When AIQ-1746 revises ES_IE durations, test_permit_corridors_have_the_measured_runway will fail with a message telling the executor to update the expectation — that is intended, not a regression.

### What the reviewer should do
1. Merge #1710 first, then retarget/merge #1711.
2. Sanity-check MIN_MATERIAL_LEAD_DAYS=7 and TIGHT_BUFFER_DAYS=14 — the only two tunables introduced.

rows.notes:
## ⚠️ RECORD CORRECTED 2026-08-04 — a claimed deliverable was never merged

This task was closed Done claiming TWO created files. Only ONE reached main. The
deliverable-integrity CI guard caught it, and was failing on every open PR repo-wide
until this correction.

### Files changed
- CREATED: docs/form-autofill/ACROFORM-FEASIBILITY-DE-FR.md — evidence, split verdict, consequences. On main (87 lines).
- REMOVED: the FR AcroForm field dump fields_FR_cerfa_14571-05.txt was listed here as created. It does NOT exist in the repo and never did — PR #1743 (e1af737a) shipped exactly one file, and nothing matching cerfa or 14571 is anywhere on main (verified with git ls-tree -r origin/main). The claim is withdrawn.

### Two criteria were recorded as passing and were not

Criterion 5 ("field dump committed — done for FR"): FALSE. The dump is not in the
repo. Corrected to NOT MET below.

Criterion 1 ("enumerates 172 AcroForm fields. PASSES"): CANNOT BE CONFIRMED, and
#1743's own commit body says the opposite — "Not verified: the France-Visas
cerfa_14571-05 FR/EN/ES variants were not field-tested. If one is a genuine AcroForm the

rows.title: Add destination dropdowns with missing-destination request flow
rows.notes:
## What shipped (PR #1610, merged — commit 6ae5b630)
Catalogue-backed destination fields + a 'request a destination we don't support yet' flow, across BOTH the employee intake and the HR company profile. Built by a parallel session; this dev-queue session made the product call, verified it end-to-end, and merged it.

## Product decision (Romain, this session): NEVER-BLOCK
The catalogue (catalog_destination_allowlist) is only 75 cities / 28 countries (verified via SQL), so a hard closed dropdown would block most real relocations. Chosen design: fields stay typeable, seed searchable suggestions from the live catalogue, and a chosen destination not in the catalogue is still accepted while firing an admin request (controlled scaling) + a confirmation.

## Files changed (all in #1610)
- backend/app/routers/employee_quotes.py — new GET /api/employee/destinations (require_hr_or_employee) → scrape_safety.list_allowlist(); rides the router registered in both apps.
- frontend/src/api/destinations.ts (new) — listEmployeeDestinations() + requestDestination(city, country, notes?), role-agnostic. Wires the previously-uncalled POST /api/employee/destination-request.
- frontend/src/components/Combobox.tsx (new) — shared searchable combobox: suggests from options, never blocks a typed value (4 unit tests).
- frontend/src/features/platform-v2/intake/EmployeeIntakePage.tsx — CityCombo seeds from the live catalogue (fallback to static); leaving step 1 fires the request for an out-of-catalogue dest city (deduped) + persistent confirmation banner.
- frontend/src/pages/HrCompanyProfile.tsx — Country + Default destination country → full-country-list Combobox; HQ city + Default working location → catalogue-cities Combobox scoped by the paired country; request fires on SAVE for an out-of-catalogue working location + confirmation.

## Validation results
- ✅ Verified PR #1610 on a clean checkout: tsc --noEmit clean; vitest run intake → 47 passed; GET /api/employee/destinations present in the prod app instance; Combobox 4 tests pass.
- ✅ CI green (frontend build/types/lint/unit + backend P1 + route-auth) before merge.
- ✅ Persistence-safe: HR profile fields keep string (name) values — the save payload keys (country, hq_city, default_destination_country, default_working_location) are unchanged, and countries stay stored as NAMES (not ISO codes).
- ✅ Criteria met: dropdowns/suggestions on both HR + employee flows (1,8); searchable (2); country scopes city options (3); request-if-missing without leaving the page (4); confirmation shown (5); persisted to catalog_destination_requests → visible at /admin/catalog-queue (6); no regression — intake gate + save flow unchanged (7).

## Decisions made
- Never-block over hard-gating (see above) — the 75-city catalogue makes a closed dropdown user-hostile; the request flow is the escape hatch.
- Countries use the full ISO country list (not the 28 catalogue countries) so a company's own country is never wrongly constrained; only CITIES are catalogue-scoped.

rows.title: Intake-profile overlay shows the employee ciphertext instead of falling back to their own plaintext
rows.notes:
## Fixed 2026-08-11 as part of AIQ-1802 — merged as 7eccfa03 (PR #1788)

Closed alongside the fail-open decrypt task, because it was the same code block and the same root cause. Fixing them separately would have meant two passes over the same twenty lines.

The two bugs compounded exactly as filed:
1. the overlay treated any non-null vault value as authoritative, discarding the employee's correct canonical intake value;
2. the decrypt then failed open and returned the ciphertext.

Net effect: the employee was shown an unreadable blob while the system held their own correct plaintext, discarded a few lines earlier.

Now: an undecryptable vault value is not a winning value. GET /api/employee/cases/{case_id}/profile falls back to the canonical intake value when decryption fails, and only if canonical has nothing either does it omit and return passport_number_withheld: true.

Vault-wins semantics are unchanged for every value that decrypts successfully — this was a narrow fix to the failure branch, as the task specified.

See the AIQ-1802 page for the full validation record.

rows.notes:
## Built (PR #1513) — the one real deliverable
frontend/src/components/admin/FeedbackTab.tsx: added a "Copy issue to context" button next to the per-item dispatch-context textarea. It sets contextDrafts[row.id] = row.text and persists through the same save path the textarea uses on blur. Disabled when the row has no text; distinct from the unrelated ~:77 "Copy" (which copies a CLI command).

## Deliberately NOT done (FALSE "bug" premises — these are intentional gates)
- 422 on dispatch/create is the eval quality gate (EvalGateError, score<70) and already has a force-dispatch override UI (EvalGatePanel). Removing it is a regression — left intact.
- 409 on /fix correctly means "not dispatched yet" and already shows a friendly message; the other dispatch_create 409s are concurrency sentinels — all left intact.
- No confirm-modal removal (there is no intermediate confirm modal; the flow is already single-step). No backend Pydantic/idempotency changes.

The generate→review→create chain already existed inline, so nothing new was wired there. Acceptance criteria demanding "no 409/422" are unachievable without breaking the quality gate and were intentionally not satisfied (documented).

## Validation
✅ tsc clean · build clean · eslint 0 · 17 FeedbackTab/AdminFeedback tests pass.

Marked Partial: only the legitimate ask (the button) was built; ~80% of the written task chased non-bugs.
